---
url: https://jetpack-desktop.github.io/guide/introduction.md
description: >-
  Why JetPack replaces heavy Docker/VMs with native GPU compute inside
  unprivileged OS kernel sandboxes.
---

# Introduction & Philosophy

JetPack is a cross-platform **Local Compute & Native App Orchestrator** designed to give modern web applications direct, sandboxed access to local CPU, RAM, and GPU hardware without requiring users to install Docker Desktop, virtual machines, or unmanaged Python toolchains.

## Why Browser-Only WebGPU & WASM Hit a Wall

WebAssembly (WASM) and WebGPU made significant strides in bringing computation to the browser, yet serious local AI inference, media transcoding, and native data processing encounter fundamental browser platform constraints:

| Constraint | Browser WASM / WebGPU | JetPack Native Workers |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Memory Ceiling** | `wasm32` linear memory is capped at **4 GiB** (often ~2 GiB practical allocation per tab), making 7B–70B parameter models or large video buffers impractical. | Full host physical RAM and Unified Memory (`16 GiB–192+ GiB`), plus direct dedicated GPU VRAM. |
| **GPU Ecosystem** | Limited to WebGPU/WGSL shaders; no access to vendor-tuned kernels such as **NVIDIA CUDA / cuDNN / TensorRT**, **Apple Metal / MPS / MLX**, **AMD ROCm**, or **VideoToolbox / NVENC**. | Direct native access to CUDA, Metal/MPS/MLX, ROCm, Vulkan, DirectML, and hardware video encoders when `permissions.gpu_access = true`. |
| **CPU Threading & SIMD** | Constrained by `SharedArrayBuffer` COOP/COEP headers, 128-bit WASM SIMD, and browser worker pool overhead. | Native multi-core threads, AVX2/AVX-512, NEON/AMX, and native C/C++/Rust/Python libraries. |
| **Binary Ecosystem** | Cannot run existing native binaries (`ffmpeg`, `llama.cpp`, `postgres`, PyTorch C++ extensions) without brittle Emscripten ports. | Runs unmodified multi-arch native binaries (`PE/.exe`, `Mach-O`, `ELF`) and standalone Python via `uv`. |
| **Storage & Deduplication** | Duplicated Origin-Private File System (OPFS) blobs per origin; slow multi-GB downloads. | Shared Content-Addressable Storage (`blobs/sha256/`) with OS hardlinks and macOS APFS Copy-on-Write clones. |

## Core Architectural Invariants

Every component in JetPack adheres to seven strict architectural invariants:

1. **Zero Virtual Machines**: No WSL2, Hyper-V, Apple `Virtualization.framework`, Docker Daemon, or `containerd`. Workers execute directly on the host kernel as native processes.
2. **User-Space Only (No Admin / No Root)**: Everything installs and executes inside the current unprivileged user's profile (`%APPDATA%\JetPack`, `~/Library/Application Support/JetPack`, `~/.config/jetpack`). No UAC prompts and no `sudo`.
3. **Zero System Pollution**: JetPack never writes to Windows `HKLM`, modifies global system `PATH`, installs system root CAs, or calls `/usr/bin/python3`.
4. **Rust as the Sole Gatekeeper**: Browser tabs never connect directly to Python or C++ workers. Every external WebSocket connection terminates, authenticates, and decrypts inside `jetpack-daemon` (Rust).
5. **Default-Deny OS Kernel Sandboxing**: Every worker runs inside a platform-native sandbox (`AppContainer` + `Job Objects` on Windows, `Seatbelt` on macOS, `bwrap` + `Landlock LSM` on Linux) with zero filesystem or network access unless explicitly granted.
6. **Userspace Network Proxy**: Sandboxed workers have no direct network interface. Allowed outbound `host:port` endpoints are proxied through `jetpack-daemon` according to `permissions.network_allowlist`.
7. **Zero-Copy Binary Framing**: No JSON payloads over WebSockets. Control plane and worker traffic use `[4B length] + [MsgPack Header] + [Raw Binary Payload]` protected by `X25519` + `ChaCha20-Poly1305`.

## Next Steps

* Explore the [Three-Tier Architecture & User Space Layout](/guide/architecture).
* Follow [Getting Started](/guide/getting-started) to launch `jetpack-daemon` and the Control Center.
* Review the [Security Overview](/security/overview) for a full audit of JetPack's isolation boundaries.

  Rust gatekeeper daemon, and kernel-sandboxed native/Python workers.

# Architecture & User Space

JetPack separates untrusted browser code, security enforcement, and heavy native computation into three strictly isolated tiers.

## Three-Tier System Architecture

```text
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Tier 1: Browser / WASM Frontend                                             |
|   @jetpack/client (TypeScript) -> jetpack-wasm (wasm32-unknown-unknown)     |
|   - Persistent Ed25519 / X25519 identity in localStorage                    |
|   - Out-of-Band pairing via jetpack://pair                                  |
|   - Encrypted binary WebSocket client (ws://127.0.0.1:9470)                 |
+--------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+
                                       |
                                       | 127.0.0.1:9470 (Origin + PNA + X25519
                                       | + ChaCha20-Poly1305 Binary Framing)
                                       v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Tier 2: Rust Tray Gatekeeper (jetpack-daemon)                               |
|   - Dynamic installed app UI (<root>/apps/<app-id>/<version>/ui/) &       |
|     embedded Control Center HTTP server (http://127.0.0.1:9470)             |
|   - ChaCha20-Poly1305 encrypted paired client & volume store (OS Vault key) |
|   - Ed25519 SignedAppCatalog verifier & anti-spoofing enforcer              |
|   - Hardware Discovery (NVML / Vulkan / DX12 / Metal / sysctl)              |
|   - OCI CAS Manager (blobs/sha256/) + uv Python + RuntimeProvisioner        |
|   - In-Daemon Userspace Network Proxy (permissions.network_allowlist)       |
|   - Cross-platform OS Sandbox Runner + WorkerLifecycleManager               |
+--------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+
                                       |
                                       | Local Kernel IPC (UDS 0600 / Named Pipe
                                       | with AppContainer DACL) + [4B len] frames
                                       v
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Tier 3: Sandboxed Native Workers                                            |
|   - Windows: AppContainer (Low Integrity SID) + NTFS ACLs + Job Object      |
|   - macOS:   Seatbelt (deny default) + gated AGXDeviceUserClient (Metal)    |
|   - Linux:   Bubblewrap (CLONE_NEWNET, pivot_root) + Landlock LSM           |
|   - Runtimes: standalone Python (uv), ffmpeg, llama.cpp, custom binaries    |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### Tier 1: WASM Frontend (`jetpack-wasm` & `@jetpack/client`)

Web applications (including standalone MPA/SPA UIs hosted under `/apps/<app-id>/` and third-party web frontends) interact with JetPack through the high-level `@jetpack/client` TypeScript package (`JetPackAppClient` and its auto-mounted Shadow-DOM `JetPackControlBar`) layered on top of `jetpack-wasm`. All protocol framing, `Ed25519` request signing, `X25519` key exchange, and `ChaCha20-Poly1305` encryption execute inside WebAssembly (`jetpack-proto` compiled for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`) before bytes touch the browser `WebSocket`.

### Tier 2: Rust Tray Gatekeeper (`jetpack-daemon`)

`jetpack-daemon` is a lightweight native binary (`~5–10 MB`) managing the system tray icon (`tao` + `tray-icon`), native `wry` WebView windows (with cross-platform `download_started`/`download_completed` handlers and a `blob:`/`data:` `rfd` save-dialog IPC bridge for `<a download>` and diagnostic `.zip` exports), the loopback HTTP/WebSocket server on `127.0.0.1:9470`, hardware discovery, OCI bundle caching (including slim single-example release seeding), isolated Python/native runtime provisioning, native OS dialogs (`rfd`), sanitized diagnostic bundle export/reporting (`diagnostics`), SHA-256-verified self-updates (`updater`), and worker lifecycle supervision.

For `/apps/<app-id>/` HTTP requests, `jetpack-daemon` checks `<root>/apps/<app-id>/<active_version>/ui/` first (enforcing path canonicalization and symlink-escape rejection, with MPA `<subpath>/index.html` and extensionless SPA fallback to `ui/index.html`) and falls back to the cascading Control Center bundle (`JETPACK_WEB_DIST_DIR`, `<root>/ui/dist/`, `./web/dist/`, embedded `ControlCenterAssets`) only when `<app-dir>/ui/` does not exist.

No browser client ever communicates directly with a worker socket or pipe. `jetpack-daemon` decrypts incoming WebSocket frames, authorizes the session `Origin` against the target application, and forwards plaintext hybrid frames over local kernel IPC only to the authorized worker job.

### Tier 3: Sandboxed Native Workers

Each launched job executes inside a dedicated per-job workspace (`<root>/workspaces/job_<uuid>`) under strict OS kernel confinement. Workers receive:

* `JETPACK_IPC_ENDPOINT`: local Unix Domain Socket (`ipc.sock`) or Windows Named Pipe (`\\.\pipe\jetpack-worker-<job_id>`).
* `JETPACK_PROXY_ENDPOINT` / `HTTP_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY`: userspace network proxy endpoint when `permissions.network_allowlist` is non-empty.
* `JETPACK_VOL_<NAME>`: sandbox-mounted paths for user-selected host folders declared in `volumes.<name>`.
* Hermetic `PATH` prepended with `<root>/runtimes/<name>-<version>/bin` for declared `runtimes` dependencies.

## User-Space Directory Layout (`JetPackPaths`)

Implemented in `crates/jetpack-common/src/paths.rs`, JetPack keeps all configuration, caches, runtimes, and job workspaces strictly inside the unprivileged user's profile:

| Platform | Default Root Path |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Windows (`windows/amd64`)** | `%APPDATA%\JetPack` |
| **macOS (`darwin/arm64`)** | `~/Library/Application Support/JetPack` |
| **Linux (`linux/amd64`)** | `~/.config/jetpack` |

You can override the root directory hermetically for testing or portable installations using the `JETPACK_HOME` environment variable (legacy `CORENODE_HOME` is also recognized as a fallback). On first startup, `JetPackPaths::init_dirs()` automatically migrates legacy `CoreNode` directories if present and enforces mode `0700` on Unix directories.

```text
<JETPACK_ROOT>/
├── config/
│   ├── daemon.toml              # Daemon bind address, port, logging, updates, and diagnostics configuration
│   ├── paired_clients.db        # ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD encrypted SQLite DB (paired clients, authorized_volumes, settings)
│   └── pairing.ipc              # Local IPC socket/metadata for single-instance URI forwarding
├── logs/
│   ├── daemon.log               # Persistent UTF-8 tracing log (redacted in diagnostic exports)
│   └── jetpack-diagnostics-*.zip# Optional user-exported sanitized diagnostic bundles
├── webview-data/                # Persistent wry WebView storage (localStorage pairing keys & cache)
├── blobs/
│   └── sha256/
│       ├── <hex>                # Content-Addressable OCI layer/config/manifest blobs
│       └── <hex>.unpacked/      # Tar-Slip-verified unpacked layer directories
├── runtimes/
│   ├── uv/                      # Portable uv binary
│   ├── python/                  # Managed python-build-standalone distributions
│   └── <name>-<version>/bin/    # Verified shared native runtimes (e.g., ffmpeg-9.0.2)
├── apps/
│   └── <app-id>/<version>/      # Deduplicated app bundles (hardlinks / APFS clones), optional ui/ static bundle, and .venv
├── workspaces/
│   └── job_<uuid>/              # Ephemeral per-job sandbox RW directory + ipc.sock
├── updates/                     # Verified release downloads, SHA256SUMS.txt, and staging dirs (mode 0700)
└── cache/
    └── uv/                      # Shared zero-duplication wheel cache (UV_CACHE_DIR, mode 0700)
```

## Monorepo Crate & Package Layout

| Path | Role |
| :--- | :--- |
| `crates/jetpack-proto` | `wasm32`-compatible crate for `HybridFrame`, `X25519`/`Ed25519` handshake, `ChaCha20-Poly1305` cipher, pairing URIs, and `HardwareProfile` / control-plane schemas |
| `crates/jetpack-common` | `AppManifest` (`app.toml`) strict parser/validator, `DaemonConfig`, `JetPackPaths`, and shared errors |
| `crates/jetpack-daemon` | Tray agent, `127.0.0.1:9470` WS/Control Center + standalone MPA server, ChaCha20-Poly1305 encrypted SQLite store (`rusqlite` `bundled`), pure-Rust TLS (`rustls-tls`), OCI/Python/runtime provisioners, OS sandboxes, and CLI tools |
| `crates/jetpack-wasm` | `wasm-bindgen` browser SDK (`WasmClientIdentity`, `JetPackWasmClient`) |
| `web/` | Embedded Control Center UI, standalone MPA web apps (`web/apps/*` -> `web/dist/`), and `@jetpack/client` TypeScript SDK (`web/packages/jetpack-client`) |
| `sdks/python/jetpack_sdk` | Lightweight Python worker IPC library (`JetPackClient`, `HybridFrame`, zero-copy reader) |

  Build jetpack-daemon and the jetpack CLI, probe host GPUs, start the tray
  daemon, and open Control Center on 127.0.0.1:9470.

# Getting Started

This guide walks through building `jetpack-daemon`, inspecting your host hardware profile, starting the background tray daemon, and opening the embedded **Control Center** at `http://127.0.0.1:9470`.

## Prerequisites

* **Rust 1.75+** (stable toolchain) with the WebAssembly target:
  ```bash
  rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
  ```
* **Node.js 20+** and `npm` (for building the WASM bindings and Control Center UI, or running the documentation portal).
* **Platform notes**:
  * **Windows (`windows/amd64`)**: Standard user account; no Administrator / UAC elevation required.
  * **macOS (`darwin/arm64`)**: Apple Silicon with Xcode Command Line Tools (`Metal.framework` is detected automatically).
  * **Linux (`linux/amd64`)**: `bubblewrap` (`bwrap`) installed with unprivileged user namespaces enabled, plus a kernel supporting Landlock LSM (`Linux 5.13+`).

## 1. Build the Daemon, CLI, and Embedded Control Center

Build the WASM client, compile the Control Center frontend (`web/dist/`), and produce both `jetpack-daemon` and the `jetpack` CLI (including `jetpack mcp`) release binaries:

```bash
make web-install
make release-daemon
```

Or run the debug workspace build during development:

```bash
cargo build --workspace
```

## 2. Verify Host Hardware Discovery

Probe your CPU topology, system/unified memory, and GPU adapters (`NVML` / `Vulkan` / `DX12` / `Metal`) directly in user space:

```bash
./target/debug/jetpack-daemon --print-hardware-profile
```

Example output on Apple Silicon:

```text
JetPack Hardware Profile (macos/aarch64)
  CPU:    Apple M1 Pro (10 physical / 10 logical cores, 8P + 2E)
  Memory: 16384 MiB total / 3241 MiB available (unified=true, recommended_max_working_set=12124 MiB)
  GPUs (1 detected):
    [0] Apple M1 Pro | vendor=Apple | backend=Metal | driver=Metal | vram=12124 MiB total (3241 MiB free) | unified=true
```

## 3. Start the Daemon and Open Control Center

Launch `jetpack-daemon`:

```bash
RUST_LOG=info ./target/release/jetpack-daemon
```

*(For headless CI or SSH environments without a desktop system tray, pass `--headless`. OS autostart entries configured via **Launch at Login** pass `--background` silently so the dashboard does not pop up on every OS reboot.)*

When started:

1. `JetPackPaths::init_dirs()` initializes your isolated user-space directory (`0700` on Unix).
2. `jetpack-daemon` registers the `jetpack://` custom URI scheme in user space (`HKCU\Software\Classes` on Windows, `~/.local/share/applications/jetpack-daemon.desktop` on Linux, bundle `Info.plist` on macOS).
3. The system tray icon appears in the OS menu bar / notification area with quick status and shortcuts.
4. The loopback gatekeeper and embedded Control Center start listening strictly on `127.0.0.1:9470`.
5. When launched interactively (without `--background` or `--headless`) and `open_dashboard_on_startup` is `true` (default), `jetpack-daemon` automatically opens `http://127.0.0.1:9470`—either in a dedicated native WebView window (`open_in_app_window = true`) or in your default browser. You can toggle this preference anytime under **My Hardware & Security -> Window & Launch Mode ("Open Control Center on startup")**.

You can also open the Control Center manually at:

```text
http://127.0.0.1:9470
```

From the Control Center you can:

* Inspect live CPU, RAM, and GPU telemetry (`hardware.get_profile`).
* Browse and install verified applications from the `Ed25519`-signed **App Store** (`SignedAppCatalog`). Official release installers pre-bundle only the slimmed `examples/ffmpeg-media-converter` starter worker (`io.jetpack.media-converter`) to minimize installer size, while other services are downloaded on demand from the catalog.
* Launch standalone web apps in a dedicated browser tab (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:9470/apps/io.jetpack.media-converter/` with the integrated `JetPackControlBar`) or manage/terminate installed apps, reset cached volume folder authorizations, and monitor local developer apps (`UNVERIFIED / LOCAL DEV`) in **My Apps & Activity**.
* Review and revoke paired browser origins (`paired_clients.db`).
* Export a secret-redacted `.zip` diagnostic bundle (`diagnostics.json` + bounded `daemon.log` tail) from **My Hardware & Security -> Diagnostics & Support Logs**, the system tray (**"Export Diagnostics..."**), or CLI (`jetpack-daemon --export-diagnostics`). Optional HTTP JSON reporting is disabled by default (`[diagnostics].report_url = None` in `daemon.toml`) and enforces `https://` (or loopback `http://` for local testing) with bounded `request_timeout_secs` (`1..=60`).
* Check for and apply verified `jetpack-daemon` releases from **My Hardware & Security -> JetPack Updates** or the system tray (**"Check for Updates..."** / **"Update Available: vX.Y.Z"**), configured via `[updates]` in `daemon.toml` (`release_api_url`, `auto_check = true`, `check_interval_hours = 12`).

## 4. Run Built-In Verification Smoke Tests

Before connecting an external web app or publishing workers, you can verify the entire local security stack offline:

```bash
# 1. Verify 127.0.0.1 binding, PNA headers, X25519/Ed25519 handshake, ChaCha20-Poly1305 & 1003 JSON rejection
./target/debug/jetpack-daemon --ws-smoke-test

# 2. Verify OCI multi-arch CAS & hardlink/APFS clone deduplication
./target/debug/jetpack-daemon --oci-smoke-test

# 3. Verify isolated uv + python-build-standalone provisioner
./target/debug/jetpack-daemon --python-smoke-test

# 4. Verify OS native kernel sandbox (AppContainer / Seatbelt / bwrap+Landlock)
./target/debug/jetpack-daemon --sandbox-smoke-test

# 5. Verify sandboxed worker IPC, userspace network proxy & lifecycle cleanup
./target/debug/jetpack-daemon --worker-ipc-smoke-test
```

## Next Steps

* Connect a web app using the [@jetpack/client Quickstart](/sdk/frontend/quickstart).
* Scaffold your first Python worker with `--init-app` in the [CLI Tools Reference](/publishing/cli-tools).
* Inspect the cryptographic and sandbox guarantees in [Security Overview](/security/overview).

# AI Agents & MCP Integration

JetPack includes a complete AI-Agent Developer Experience (DX) suite designed so coding agents (**Claude Code**, **Cursor**, **Windsurf**, **OpenClaw**, and custom MCP clients) can scaffold, type-check, validate, and debug `@jetpack/client` + Python Worker applications with zero hallucinations.

## 1. LLM-Friendly Documentation (`llms.txt` & `llms-full.txt`)

Every JetPack documentation build publishes clean, HTML-free Markdown entry points at the root of the static site:

* **`https://jetpack-desktop.github.io/llms.txt`** — Structured index of all Guide, Security Audit, Frontend SDK, Worker SDK, and Publishing & CLI pages with 1-line summaries.
* **`https://jetpack-desktop.github.io/llms-full.txt`** — Single concatenated Markdown document containing the entire JetPack documentation set.

### Linking Docs in AI IDEs

* **Cursor**: Open **Settings → Features → Docs → Add new doc** and enter `https://jetpack-desktop.github.io/llms-full.txt`, then reference `@JetPack` in Composer/Chat.
* **Claude Code / OpenClaw**: Fetch or reference `https://jetpack-desktop.github.io/llms.txt` to discover relevant pages, or attach `llms-full.txt` directly when working offline.
* **Offline / Local via MCP**: Use the `search_docs` tool inside `jetpack mcp` (which embeds version-matched `docs/` Markdown directly inside the `jetpack` CLI binary and supports overriding with `JETPACK_DOCS_DIR`).

## 2. Built-In Local MCP Server (`jetpack mcp`)

The standalone console CLI `jetpack` (`crates/jetpack-cli`) includes a Model Context Protocol server powered by the official `rmcp` crate over `stdio` transport (`stdin`/`stdout` JSON-RPC, with all diagnostic tracing routed strictly to `stderr`).

### Client Configuration (`mcpServers`)

Every official JetPack release bundle includes the `jetpack` CLI alongside `jetpack-daemon`, so you can point your MCP client directly at the installed binary without building from source.

Add the appropriate configuration for your OS to **Claude Code** (`.mcp.json` or `~/.claude.json`), **Cursor** (`.cursor/mcp.json` or `~/.cursor/mcp.json`), **Windsurf** (`~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json`), or any MCP-compatible IDE:

#### macOS (`darwin/arm64`)

When `JetPack.app` is installed in `/Applications`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "jetpack": {
      "command": "/Applications/JetPack.app/Contents/MacOS/jetpack",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

*(If you placed `JetPack.app` in `~/Applications`, use `/Users/<you>/Applications/JetPack.app/Contents/MacOS/jetpack`.)*

#### Windows (`windows/amd64`)

When `JetPack-windows-x64.zip` is extracted into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\JetPack\`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "jetpack": {
      "command": "C:\\Users\\<you>\\AppData\\Local\\JetPack\\jetpack.exe",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

#### Linux (`linux/amd64`)

When `JetPack-linux-x64.tar.gz` is extracted into `~/.local/opt/jetpack/`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "jetpack": {
      "command": "/home/<you>/.local/opt/jetpack/jetpack",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

#### Using `PATH` or Building from Source

If `jetpack` is on your shell `PATH` (for example via `cargo install --path crates/jetpack-cli` or a symlink in `/usr/local/bin` / `~/.local/bin`), or if you are testing an unreleased local build (`target/release/jetpack`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "jetpack": {
      "command": "jetpack",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

> **Note:** Regardless of where `jetpack` is invoked from, `jetpack mcp` automatically discovers and communicates with your active `jetpack-daemon` via `<JETPACK_HOME>/config/pairing.ipc` (including when the daemon was launched from `/Applications/JetPack.app`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\JetPack\jetpack-daemon.exe`, or `~/.local/opt/jetpack/jetpack-daemon`), and `jetpack install-local` / `jetpack package` automatically use the sibling `jetpack-daemon` binary in the same directory.

### Exposed MCP Tools

| Tool | Parameters | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `search_docs` | `query: string`, `max_results?: number` (`1..20`, default `5`) | Searches embedded version-matched JetPack documentation (or `JETPACK_DOCS_DIR`) by keyword/topic and returns ranked Markdown snippets. |
| `get_daemon_status` | *(none)* | Checks `jetpack-daemon` health, version, bound `127.0.0.1` WebSocket port, reachability, paired origins, and active sandboxed workers via token-authenticated `pairing.ipc`. |
| `read_worker_logs` | `app_id: string`, `lines?: number` (`1..2000`, default `100`) | Tails live or offline `worker.log` / `daemon.log` crash tracebacks and stdout/stderr for `app_id`, automatically redacting sensitive keys, tokens, and user paths. |
| `validate_manifest` | `path: string` | Validates `app.toml` (or a directory containing `app.toml`) against the strict `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` schema, permissions, volumes, runtimes, and `python_env`. |
| `scaffold_app` | `target_dir: string`, `app_id?: string`, `template?: "python" \| "fullstack"` (default `"fullstack"`) | Generates a starter JetPack app with `app.toml`, `worker.py`, optional `@jetpack/client` TypeScript frontend, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/rules/jetpack.mdc`, and `.agents/skills/`. |

## 3. Project Scaffolding Rules & Agent Skills (`jetpack init`)

Running `jetpack init` (or `jetpack-daemon --init-app`, or the `scaffold_app` MCP tool) generates a ready-to-run project preloaded with AI guardrails:

```bash
# Python worker starter + AI rules & skills
jetpack init ./workers/my-ocr-worker --template python

# Fullstack TypeScript (@jetpack/client) + Python worker starter
jetpack init ./apps/my-ai-app --app-id com.dev.my-ai-app --template fullstack
```

### Generated AI Artifacts

* **`AGENTS.md`** — Canonical instructions enforcing `JetPackAppClient.connectAndEnsureApp()`, strict MsgPack metadata vs zero-copy `Uint8Array` payload separation, frontend-to-worker opcode parity, and `app.toml` security rules.
* **`CLAUDE.md`** — Regular-file mirror of `AGENTS.md` (not a symlink, ensuring full compatibility on Windows and OCI layer packaging).
* **`.cursor/rules/jetpack.mdc`** — Cursor MDC rule file auto-attaching JetPack architecture constraints.
* **`.agents/skills/`** — Step-by-step reusable Agent Skills:
  * `.agents/skills/create-jetpack-worker/SKILL.md` — Scaffolding, manifest setup, `jetpack validate`, and local installation.
  * `.agents/skills/add-binary-opcode/SKILL.md` — Adding a Pydantic/typed Python worker handler, regenerating `jetpack-env.d.ts`, and calling it from `@jetpack/client`.
  * `.agents/skills/debug-pairing/SKILL.md` — Diagnosing `127.0.0.1:9470` WebSocket pairing, `jetpack://pair` OOB approval, and worker launch errors via MCP.

All AI instruction files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `.agents/`) and generated `jetpack-env.d.ts` declarations are automatically excluded when packaging OCI bundles via `jetpack package` or `jetpack-daemon --package-app`.

## 4. End-to-End Agentic Workflow with `jetpack codegen`

To eliminate frontend/worker opcode drift and metadata typos, define your Python worker schemas with Pydantic `BaseModel`, `TypedDict`, or `@dataclass`, and optionally annotate handlers with `@opcode` (or `client.opcode(...)`) from `jetpack_sdk`:

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel
from jetpack_sdk import JetPackClient, opcode


class TranscribeRequest(BaseModel):
    language: str = "en"
    diarize: bool = False


class TranscribeResponse(BaseModel):
    text: str
    duration_ms: int


@opcode("audio.transcribe", request=TranscribeRequest, response=TranscribeResponse, binary=True)
def handle_transcribe(client: JetPackClient, meta: TranscribeRequest, payload: bytes):
    return {"text": "ok", "duration_ms": len(payload)}
```

Generate strict TypeScript declarations from the worker AST (without executing Python):

```bash
jetpack codegen --worker worker.py --out src/jetpack-env.d.ts --strict
```

Then pass `JetPackOpcodeMap` as the generic parameter to `JetPackAppClient`:

```typescript
import { JetPackAppClient } from '@jetpack/client';
import type { JetPackOpcodeMap } from './jetpack-env';

const client = new JetPackAppClient<JetPackOpcodeMap>();
await client.connectAndEnsureApp({ appId: 'com.dev.my-ai-app', daemonPort: 9470 });

// Compile-time checked by tsc: opcode name, meta shape, required Uint8Array, and response type
const reply = await client.request('audio.transcribe', { language: 'en' }, audioBytes);
```

If an agent invents a nonexistent opcode, forgets the required `Uint8Array` payload when `binary: true`, or misspells a metadata field, `tsc --noEmit` fails immediately so the agent can self-correct before runtime.

---
url: https://jetpack-desktop.github.io/security/overview.md
description: >-
  Threat model and four-layer defense-in-depth boundaries protecting loopback
  127.0.0.1 compute from untrusted web origins.
---

# Security Overview

JetPack exposes local native hardware and OS-level compute to web applications running inside untrusted browser origins. Because a local daemon listening on `127.0.0.1` is an attractive target for malicious websites, DNS rebinding, browser extensions, and supply-chain tampering, JetPack enforces defense-in-depth across four distinct security boundaries.

## Threat Model & Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Threat Addressed | Enforcement Mechanism |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Browser <-> Daemon Transport** | Cross-site WebSocket hijacking, DNS rebinding, rogue local tabs, plaintext inspection | Strict `127.0.0.1` bind, HTTP Upgrade `Origin` allowlist + W3C PNA, Out-of-Band `jetpack://pair` + native OS dialog, `X25519` + `Ed25519` handshake, `ChaCha20-Poly1305` encrypted framing, `1003` close on JSON/text frames |
| **2. At-Rest Credential & Consent Store** | Local unprivileged malware or SQLite tools reading paired keys or authorized folder paths | 256-bit `ChaCha20-Poly1305` (AEAD) encrypted SQLite container (`paired_clients.db`) with master key stored exclusively in OS Vault (`DPAPI` / `Keychain` / `Secret Service`), Unix `0700` / `0600` directory and file permissions |
| **3. Daemon <-> Native Worker Sandbox** | Malicious or compromised AI/media worker reading user documents (`~/Documents`, `~/.ssh`), spawning hidden background processes, or exfiltrating data over the internet | Default-deny OS kernel sandboxes (`Windows AppContainer + Job Objects`, `macOS Seatbelt`, `Linux bwrap + Landlock LSM`), user-selected `[volumes]` via native OS `rfd` picker, and an in-daemon Userspace Network Proxy filtered by `permissions.network_allowlist` |
| **4. App Store & Supply Chain** | Tampered catalog entries, App ID spoofing (`io.jetpack.*`), registry redirection, Tar-Slip extraction, linker injection (`LD_PRELOAD`) | Compiled-in `CATALOG_VERIFY_PUBKEY` (`Ed25519`), `manifest_sha256` pinning, per-app `allowed_origins` enforcement, SHA-256 CAS verification, Tar-Slip rejection, and `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` manifest validation |

## Architectural Security Guarantees

### Rust as the Sole Gatekeeper

Browser code (`@jetpack/client` / `jetpack-wasm`) **never** opens sockets or named pipes directly to Python or C++ workers. All external traffic terminates inside `jetpack-daemon` (`crates/jetpack-daemon/src/ws_server.rs`), which:

1. Refuses to bind to `0.0.0.0`, `::`, or any non-loopback IP address before opening a TCP listener.
2. Validates the normalized HTTP `Origin` header on both `OPTIONS` Private Network Access preflights and WebSocket `GET` upgrades against `paired_clients.db` (or the daemon's own Control Center origin `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`). Rejects unknown or missing origins with `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden`.
3. Enforces a 5-second post-upgrade cryptographic `ClientHello` handshake binding the HTTP `Origin` to `ClientHello.origin` and the paired `Ed25519` public key.
4. Enforces per-application `Origin` authorization before `"app.launch"` or forwarding any frame with `target_worker` set.

### Zero Client Trust for Host Paths & Privileges

* Web clients **cannot** pass absolute host filesystem paths to workers; any path in `AppLaunchRequest` is ignored/rejected. Host folders for `[volumes.<name>]` are selected exclusively by the human user through the native OS folder dialog (`rfd`).
* Web clients **cannot** bypass `SignedAppCatalog` verification via `"settings.set"` (`developer_mode = true` never enables unverified network `"app.pull"`).
* Local developer apps (`--install-local-app`) are restricted strictly to non-official IDs (never shadowing `SignedAppCatalog` entries) and can only be invoked from loopback origins (`127.0.0.1` / `localhost`).
* Self-update execution (`"update.apply"`) is restricted exclusively to the embedded loopback Control Center origin (`is_own_loopback_origin`). Every release download enforces `https://` (or loopback `http://` for tests), strict `SHA-256` verification against `SHA256SUMS.txt` with immediate deletion on mismatch, and Zip-Slip / Tar-Slip symlink-escape rejection before replacing binaries or bundled starter apps in user space.

## Detailed Security Audit Sections

* [Pairing & Cryptography](/security/pairing-and-crypto): Out-of-Band `jetpack://pair`, `X25519` + `Ed25519` handshake, `ChaCha20-Poly1305` framing, and `ChaCha20-Poly1305` at-rest store + OS Vault key management.
* [OS Kernel Sandboxing](/security/os-sandboxing): Platform-by-platform kernel primitives (`AppContainer`, `Seatbelt`, `bwrap` + `Landlock LSM`) and Userspace Network Proxy filtering.
* [Signed Catalog & Anti-Spoofing](/security/signed-catalog): `Ed25519` root key verification, `manifest_sha256` pinning, and per-app `Origin` isolation.

url: https://jetpack-desktop.github.io/security/pairing-and-crypto.md
description: >-
  Out-of-Band jetpack://pair authorization, X25519/Ed25519 handshake,
  ChaCha20-Poly1305 session frames, and encrypted paired_clients.db storage.
---

# Pairing & Cryptography

JetPack protects the local `127.0.0.1:9470` WebSocket channel with Out-of-Band (OOB) human authorization, mutual asymmetric authentication, ephemeral forward secrecy, and encrypted at-rest key storage.

## 1. Out-of-Band Pairing (`jetpack://pair`)

Standard browser CORS is insufficient to protect a localhost daemon against DNS rebinding or rogue browser tabs. Every external origin must first pair out-of-band:

1. **Identity Generation (`WasmClientIdentity`)**:
   * In the browser, `jetpack-wasm` generates a random `UUIDv4` `client_id` and two 32-byte seeds (`Ed25519` signing key + companion `X25519` static key) using `getrandom`, persisted in `window.localStorage` (`jetpack_client_id`, `jetpack_ed25519_seed`, `jetpack_x25519_seed`).
2. **Pairing URI Construction**:
   * The client formats a deep link:
     ```text
     jetpack://pair?client_id=<uuid>&pubkey=<urlsafe-base64>&origin=<normalized-origin>
     ```
   * `crates/jetpack-proto/src/pairing.rs` validates that `client_id` is an RFC 4122 UUID, `pubkey` decodes to 32 bytes (`Ed25519`) or 64 bytes (`Ed25519` + `X25519`), and `origin` is a valid `https://` origin or loopback `http://127.0.0.1` / `http://localhost`. Plain `http://` remote origins are rejected with `PairingUriError::InvalidOrigin`. *(Legacy `corenode://pair` URIs remain accepted for backwards compatibility.)*
3. **Single-Instance IPC Dispatch**:
   * When the OS launches `jetpack-daemon` via the custom URI handler (CLI arguments on Windows/Linux or `AppleEvent` on macOS), the secondary process pings `<root>/config/pairing.ipc` (`PING <token>`). If a primary daemon is running, it forwards the URI over local IPC and exits with status `0`.
4. **Native OS Confirmation Dialog**:
   * On the main UI thread, `jetpack-daemon` displays a native OS modal dialog (`NSAlert` on macOS, `TaskDialog` on Windows, `GTK/Portal` on Linux via `rfd`) showing:
     * Requesting web `origin`
     * `client_id` UUID
     * Deterministic `SHA-256` public key fingerprint (`SHA256:XX:YY:...`)
   * Only clicking **Yes / Allow** persists the client in `paired_clients.db`. Dismissing or clicking **No** aborts without writing to disk.

## 2. Encrypted At-Rest Storage (`ChaCha20-Poly1305` + OS Secret Vault)

Approved clients, authorized folder mounts (`authorized_volumes`), and daemon settings live in `<root>/config/paired_clients.db`, encrypted at rest as a **pure-Rust `ChaCha20-Poly1305` (AEAD)** container over serialized SQLite (`rusqlite` `bundled`, zero OpenSSL dependency).

* **Master Key & AEAD Envelope**: On first run, `OsKeyringStore` (`crates/jetpack-daemon/src/pairing.rs`) generates 32 cryptographically random bytes (`256-bit` key). Every write generates a fresh 96-bit CSPRNG nonce (`getrandom`), authenticates the `JPKDB01\0` header + nonce as AAD, and atomically replaces `paired_clients.db`.
* **OS Vault Storage (`keyring`)**: The master key is never stored in plaintext config files. It is stored exclusively inside the host OS credential vault under service `io.jetpack.daemon` (with automatic migration from legacy `io.corenode.daemon`):
  * **Windows**: Windows Credential Manager / DPAPI
  * **macOS**: macOS Keychain
  * **Linux**: FreeDesktop Secret Service (`gnome-keyring` / `KWallet`)
* Attempting to inspect `paired_clients.db` with standard `sqlite3` without the vault key fails immediately with `Error: file is not a database`.

## 3. Authenticated `X25519` + `Ed25519` Session Handshake

Every WebSocket connection to `ws://127.0.0.1:9470` must pass two layers before any application data is processed:

1. **HTTP Upgrade & Private Network Access (PNA)**:
   * On `OPTIONS` preflight and `GET` WebSocket Upgrade, `ws_server.rs` normalizes the HTTP `Origin` header and verifies it against `paired_clients.db` (or the daemon's own Control Center origin `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`).
   * Unauthorized or missing origins receive `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden`.
   * Authorized origins receive `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <origin>`, `Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network: true`, and `Vary: Origin`.
2. **Post-Upgrade `ClientHello` / `ServerHello` (`crates/jetpack-proto/src/handshake.rs`)**:
   * Immediately after `101 Switching Protocols`, the client has **5 seconds** (`DEFAULT_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT`) to send a binary `ClientHello` envelope:
     ```text
     [Magic "CNOD" (4 B)] + [Version u16 LE (2 B)] + [MsgPack ClientHello]
     ```
     *(Wire magic `"CNOD"` and transcript signing domain `b"CORENODE-HANDSHAKE-V1"` are preserved for protocol compatibility.)*
   * `ClientHello` contains `client_id`, `origin`, a fresh ephemeral `X25519` public key (`32 B`), a random `client_nonce` (`32 B`), and a 64-byte `Ed25519` signature over the transcript.
   * `ServerHandshake` verifies:
     1. `client_id` exists in `paired_clients.db`.
     2. `ClientHello.origin` matches **both** the stored `origin` in `paired_clients.db` and the HTTP Upgrade `Origin` header (preventing cross-client origin spoofing).
     3. The `Ed25519` signature is valid under the stored public key.
   * The daemon generates its own ephemeral `X25519` keypair and `server_nonce`, computes the ECDH shared secret, and derives three 256-bit secrets via **HKDF-SHA256** bound to the full handshake transcript:
     * `client_to_daemon_key` (`32 B`)
     * `daemon_to_client_key` (`32 B`)
     * `confirm_key` (`32 B`) + `session_id`
   * The daemon responds with `ServerHello` containing an `HMAC-SHA256` transcript confirmation tag (`confirm_key`), and both sides zeroize ephemeral private keys and raw shared secrets in memory (`zeroize::Zeroize`).

## 4. `ChaCha20-Poly1305` Streaming Frames & Replay Protection

After `ServerHello`, all WebSocket messages are authenticated and encrypted with `ChaCha20-Poly1305` (RFC 8439) inside `SessionCipher` (`crates/jetpack-proto/src/framing.rs`):

```text
+-------------------------------+----------------------------------------+------------------------+
| seq: uint64 LE (8 B, AAD)     | Ciphertext of Plaintext HybridFrame    | Poly1305 Tag (16 B)    |
+-------------------------------+----------------------------------------+------------------------+
```

* **Directional 96-bit Nonces**:
  * Client -> Daemon: `b"C2D\0" || seq.to_le_bytes()` (`4 B + 8 B = 12 B`)
  * Daemon -> Client: `b"D2C\0" || seq.to_le_bytes()` (`4 B + 8 B = 12 B`)
* **Associated Data (AAD)**: The 8-byte little-endian `seq` is passed as AAD to AEAD encryption/decryption.
* **Strict Anti-Replay Enforcement**: Both directions maintain independent `u64` sequence counters starting at `0`. Any frame arriving with an out-of-order, duplicated, or skipped `seq` is rejected with `ProtoError::InvalidSequenceNumber` without advancing the counter, and the WebSocket connection is closed immediately.
* **Strict Binary-Only Policy**: Sending any post-handshake WebSocket text/JSON frame (`Message::Text`) causes `jetpack-daemon` to immediately close the connection with `1003 Unsupported Data`.

  OS-native kernel sandboxing matrix across Windows AppContainer, macOS
  Seatbelt, and Linux Bubblewrap + Landlock with userspace network proxy.
---

# OS Kernel Sandboxing & Network Isolation

JetPack runs native host processes without virtual machines by confining every primary worker (`[execution]`) and companion service (`[services.<name>]`) inside an operating-system kernel sandbox. If no sandbox implementation exists for the host OS, worker launch fails with `JetPackError::SandboxError` before any process is spawned.

## Cross-Platform Kernel Sandbox Matrix

| Security Dimension | Windows (`windows/amd64`) | macOS (`darwin/arm64`) | Linux (`linux/amd64`) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Kernel Mechanism** | **AppContainer** (`CreateAppContainerProfile`) + **Low Integrity SID** | **Apple Seatbelt** (`sandbox_init` with inline SBPL `(deny default)`) | Unprivileged **Bubblewrap (`bwrap`)** namespaces + **Landlock LSM** (`SYS_LANDLOCK_RESTRICT_SELF` via `sandbox-landlock-exec`) |
| **Process Tree Cleanup** | Win32 **Job Object** with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` | Process group `killpg` (`SIGKILL` after grace period) | Namespace / PID isolation + `killpg` cleanup |
| **Job Workspace Access** | Explicit NTFS DACL (`SetNamedSecurityInfoW`) granting Read/Write on `<root>/workspaces/job_<id>` | SBPL `file-read*` + `file-write*` limited to `<root>/workspaces/job_<id>` | `--bind` + Landlock RW rule on `<root>/workspaces/job_<id>` |
| **Isolated App Home** (`JETPACK_APP_HOME`) | Explicit NTFS DACL Read/Write scoped strictly to `<appdata_root>/<app_id>` (siblings denied) | SBPL `file-read*` + `file-write*` scoped strictly to `<appdata_root>/<app_id>` (`0o700`; siblings denied) | `--bind` + Landlock RW rule scoped strictly to `<appdata_root>/<app_id>` (`0o700`; siblings denied) |
| **Shared Runtimes Access** | Explicit NTFS DACL Read-Only on `<root>/runtimes/` | SBPL `file-read*` on `<root>/runtimes/` + system libs (`/System`, `/usr/lib`, `dyld`) | `--ro-bind` + Landlock RO rule on `<root>/runtimes/` |
| **Persistent Model Cache** (`permissions.model_cache = true`) | Explicit NTFS DACL Read/Write on `<root>/cache/models` (`SUB_CONTAINERS_AND_OBJECTS_INHERIT`) | SBPL `file-read*` + `file-write*` on `<root>/cache/models` (`0o700`) | `--bind` + Landlock RW rule on `<root>/cache/models` (`0o700`) |
| **User Files (`~/Documents`, etc.)** | **Denied by default** (Low Integrity AppContainer lacks user profile ACLs) | **Denied by default** (`EPERM` / `Operation not permitted`) | **Denied by default** (`pivot_root` + Landlock LSM) |
| **Direct Host Network** | **Denied by default** (no internetClient capability granted to AppContainer) | **Denied by default** (`(deny default)` blocks outbound sockets & Mach services) | **Denied by default** (`CLONE_NEWNET` creates isolated loopback-only netns) |
| **GPU Acceleration Gate** (`permissions.gpu_access = true`) | DirectML / CUDA device access permitted inside sandbox | Conditional `(allow iokit-open (iokit-user-client-class "AGXDeviceUserClient"))` | Conditional `--dev-bind` for `/dev/dri` and `/dev/nvidia*` |
| **Cleanup on Exit** | Deletes per-job `AppContainer` profile + closes Job Object handle | Releases sandboxed child process & job workspace | Tears down `bwrap` mounts & kills process tree |

## Default-Deny Policy & `app.toml` Permissions

When `[permissions]` is omitted from `app.toml`, JetPack applies strict defaults:

```toml
[permissions]
filesystem_scopes = []
network_allowlist = []
gpu_access = false
model_cache = false
```

* **No absolute host paths**: Manifest validation rejects any path containing `..`, leading `/`, Windows drive prefixes, or `~` in `filesystem_scopes`.
* **No dynamic linker hijacking**: `[execution].env` and `[services.<name>].env` reject `LD_PRELOAD`, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `LD_AUDIT`, `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`, `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `DYLD_FRAMEWORK_PATH`, `PYTHONINSPECT`, and `PYTHONPATH`.
* **Guaranteed VRAM/RAM reclamation**: When a user explicitly stops a worker, a WebSocket session disconnects, or `jetpack-daemon` shuts down, `WorkerLifecycleManager` sends a termination signal and forcefully reaps the entire process tree after `graceful_shutdown_secs` (`10s` default), releasing GPU VRAM immediately. Workers remain active until explicitly stopped by the user or session/daemon teardown.

## Local IPC & Userspace Network Proxy

Because sandboxed workers have **no direct access to host network interfaces**, outbound traffic is brokered exclusively by `jetpack-daemon`:

### 1. Kernel-Authenticated Local IPC

* **macOS & Linux**: Unix Domain Socket at `<root>/workspaces/job_<id>/ipc.sock` with strict `0o600` file permissions.
* **Windows**: Named Pipe `\\.\pipe\jetpack-worker-<job_id>` configured with an explicit DACL allowing only the current user SID and the job's dedicated AppContainer SID (`S-1-15-2-...`).

### 2. Userspace Network Proxy (`permissions.network_allowlist`)

`jetpack-daemon` runs an asynchronous userspace HTTP/CONNECT and SOCKS5 proxy exposed to the worker via `JETPACK_PROXY_ENDPOINT` (plus `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY`):

1. **Allowlist & Preset Matching**: Every outbound `CONNECT`, plain HTTP, or SOCKS5 request checks the destination `host:port` against `permissions.network_allowlist` in `app.toml` (supports exact matches like `api.openai.com:443`, multi-label wildcard subdomains like `*.huggingface.co:443` / `*.xethub.hf.co:443`, bracketed IPv6 literals, and the `"preset:huggingface"` shorthand).
2. **Forbidden Rules**: Global wildcards (`*`, `*:*`, `0.0.0.0:*`), unknown `preset:*` tokens, and loopback daemon ports (`127.0.0.1:9470`) are rejected at manifest validation time (`crates/jetpack-common/src/manifest.rs`) or proxy evaluation time.
3. **Zero-Buffering Multi-GB Streaming**: Upstream `TcpStream::connect` uses a `30s` connect timeout while bidirectional tunnels stream with bounded `64 KiB` directional buffers (`copy_bidirectional_with_sizes`) and no overall transfer timeout so large AI model downloads complete uninterrupted. Request headers up to `64 KiB` are supported (`431 Request Header Fields Too Large` on overflow), and plain HTTP requests enforce `Connection: close` across hops.
4. **Blocking & Audit Logging**: Requests to unlisted domains are rejected immediately with `403 Forbidden` (including `X-Jetpack-Blocked-Target: <host>:<port>`) before opening any upstream TCP socket, and an actionable `WARN` event with exact `app.toml` allowlist suggestions is written to `daemon.log` and streamed to the Developer Mode terminal. Raw `connect()` syscalls bypassing the proxy fail at the kernel level (`ENETUNREACH`, `EPERM`, or `WSAEACCES`).

url: https://jetpack-desktop.github.io/security/signed-catalog.md
description: >-
  Ed25519 SignedAppCatalog verification, SHA-256 OCI CAS digest enforcement, and
  local dev anti-spoofing guarantees.
---

# Signed Catalog & Anti-Spoofing

JetPack enforces a hard security boundary between **Verified App Store Catalog** applications and **Local Unverified Developer** applications (`crates/jetpack-daemon/src/catalog.rs`).

## 1. Embedded Platform Root Key (`CATALOG_VERIFY_PUBKEY`)

`jetpack-daemon` compiles in the platform's 32-byte `Ed25519` verifying public key (`CATALOG_VERIFY_PUBKEY`) alongside the embedded base `SignedAppCatalog` (`crates/jetpack-daemon/assets/catalog.signed.json`).

* Outside `#[cfg(test)]`, `CATALOG_VERIFY_PUBKEY` is strictly immutable and cannot be overridden by `daemon.toml`, environment variables, or WebSocket control-plane opcodes.
* Before trusting any catalog entry (remote, cached, or embedded), `SignedAppCatalog::from_signed_json_and_verify` computes the canonical payload bytes (`SignedAppCatalog::canonical_payload_bytes()`, covering `version`, ordered `apps` entries, and `coming_soon`) and verifies `ed25519_signature` using `ed25519-dalek`.
* Any tampering with `oci_reference`, `manifest_sha256`, `allowed_origins`, `launch_url`, `poster_url`, `coming_soon`, `version`, or `min_vram_mb`—or a signature produced by an untrusted keypair—fails immediately with `JetPackError::CatalogSignatureInvalid`. Optional `poster_url` values must use `'self'`-relative paths (`/posters/...` without `..` or `//`) or `https://` URLs without userinfo.

## 2. Remote Catalog Refresh, Verified Caching & Offline Fallback

`DaemonConfig` (`<root>/config/daemon.toml`) configures an optional top-level `catalog_url` defaulting to `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jetpack-io/jetpack/main/crates/jetpack-daemon/assets/catalog.signed.json` (setting `catalog_url = ""` disables remote fetches cleanly for air-gapped setups). Non-empty URLs must use `https://` (or loopback `http://127.0.0.1` / `localhost` / `::1` for local testing).

When an authenticated client requests `"catalog.get"`:

1. **Bounded HTTPS Fetch**: The daemon asynchronously fetches `catalog.signed.json` with a strict **3-second** timeout and a 2 MiB response size cap via `reqwest` (`rustls-tls`).
2. **Signature & Anti-Rollback Check**: The remote payload must verify against `CATALOG_VERIFY_PUBKEY` and have `remote.version >= embedded.version`.
3. **Atomic Cache Persistence**: Validated catalogs are atomically written to `<root>/config/catalog.cached.json` (`0600` permissions on Unix).
4. **Transparent Fallback**: If the network is unreachable, times out, returns an error, or presents a tampered/rolled-back payload, the existing cache is **never** overwritten and the daemon transparently falls back to the last verified `<root>/config/catalog.cached.json` (if valid and `cached.version >= embedded.version`) or the compiled-in `EMBEDDED_SIGNED_CATALOG_JSON`.

## 3. Verified Network Pulls, `coming_soon` & Digest Pinning

When an authenticated client invokes `"app.pull"`:

1. **Catalog-Only Network Pulls**: The daemon resolves `app_id` or `oci_reference` exclusively against the active verified `SignedAppCatalog`. Any request targeting an unlisted image returns `"app.error"` with code `UNVERIFIED_APP_BLOCKED` without contacting any remote registry.
2. **`coming_soon` Availability Enforcement**: Announced future catalog entries marked `coming_soon: true` (rendered in the Control Center Store with a non-interactive **Coming Soon** badge) are rejected on `"app.pull"` with `PROVISIONING_FAILED` before contacting any OCI registry.
3. **No Browser Privilege Escalation**: Even if `"settings.set"` toggles `developer_mode = true`, browser WebSocket sessions are **never** permitted to pull unverified OCI references from the network.
4. **Immutable Digest & Reference Pinning**: Client-supplied registry URLs, tags, or digest overrides are ignored. The daemon pulls strictly from `CatalogAppEntry.oci_reference` and verifies that the resolved OCI manifest digest matches `CatalogAppEntry.manifest_sha256`.
5. **Inner Manifest App ID Verification**: After unpacking the OCI layer (with Tar-Slip path traversal checks), the daemon verifies that `app.toml`'s `[package].id` matches `CatalogAppEntry.app_id`. Mismatches are rejected with `APP_SPOOFING_DETECTED` or `PROVISIONING_FAILED` before materializing into `<root>/apps/`.

## 4. Anti-Spoofing for Local Developer Apps vs. Curated Offline Seeding

Developers can install custom local workers on their own machine using the CLI (`jetpack-daemon --install-local-app <dir>`):

* **Official ID Protection**: If a local app's `app.toml` attempts to use an `app_id` reserved in `SignedAppCatalog` (such as `io.jetpack.media-converter`), `--install-local-app` rejects it with `APP_SPOOFING_DETECTED`.
* **Verified Provenance Tracking**: Apps installed via verified catalog `"app.pull"`—or seeded strictly from the daemon's curated `examples/` allowlist (`--seed-core-apps` / first-run hook guarded by `<root>/config/.core-apps-seeded`)—carry verified provenance (`is_verified = true` in `AppInfo`). Custom local apps always report `is_verified = false` and display a yellow `UNVERIFIED / LOCAL DEV` badge in the Control Center and system tray.

## 5. Per-Application WebSocket `Origin` Authorization

Having a paired WebSocket session does **not** grant a web origin access to every installed worker on the user's machine. Before `"app.launch"` or forwarding any `HybridFrame` with `target_worker` set, `jetpack-daemon` checks:

| App Provenance | Authorized WebSocket `Origin`s | Unauthorized Result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Verified Catalog App** (`is_verified = true`) | Normalized origins listed in `CatalogAppEntry.allowed_origins` **OR** the embedded Control Center origin (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>`) | Rejected with `"app.error"` code `ORIGIN_NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_APP` |
| **Local Developer App** (`is_verified = false`) | Loopback HTTP origins only (`http://127.0.0.1[:port]`, `http://localhost[:port]`) | Rejected with `"app.error"` code `ORIGIN_NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_APP` |

Remote paired origins (e.g. `https://app.example.com`) can never launch or send IPC frames to unverified local-dev workers, nor can one catalog app's origin invoke another catalog app's worker unless explicitly authorized in `allowed_origins`.

description: >-
  Connect, auto-pair, provision workers, and exchange zero-copy binary frames
  from browser TypeScript with @jetpack/client.
---

# Frontend Quickstart (`@jetpack/client`)

The `@jetpack/client` TypeScript package (`web/packages/jetpack-client`) provides `JetPackAppClient`, a high-level wrapper over `jetpack-wasm` that automates cryptographic identity management, Out-of-Band `jetpack://pair` onboarding, catalog pulls, worker launch, correlated binary requests, and streaming event subscriptions.

## Installation

Install `@jetpack/client` from NPM in any Vite, TypeScript, or modern ESM web project:

```bash
npm install @jetpack/client
```

`@jetpack/client` **bundles the compiled `jetpack-wasm` WebAssembly binary and JS glue directly inside the package** (`@jetpack/client/wasm`). External applications work out-of-the-box with zero manual WASM copying or path overrides—both `vite dev` (dependency pre-bundling) and `vite build` resolve the bundled `.wasm` module automatically.

If you host the `.wasm` binary on a custom CDN path or supply pre-loaded bindings, you can still pass `wasmModule`, `wasmModulePath`, or `wasmBinaryOrUrl` to `connectAndEnsureApp()`. To access low-level bindings directly, import from the `@jetpack/client/wasm` subpath export.

## 1. Connect, Pair, Pull, and Launch in One Call

```typescript
import { JetPackAppClient, JetPackClientError } from '@jetpack/client';

const client = new JetPackAppClient();

try {
  await client.connectAndEnsureApp({
    appId: 'io.jetpack.media-converter',
    daemonPort: 9470,
    downloadUrl: 'https://github.com/jetpack-desktop/releases/releases/latest',
    controlBar: {
      appName: 'FFmpeg Media Converter',
      warnOnUnsavedWork: () => hasActiveUnsavedWork(),
      stopConfirmTitle: 'Stop Media Converter?',
      stopConfirmMessage: 'Transcoding is active. Stopping the worker will lose progress.',
      onBeforeStop: async () => {
        // Optional extra async cleanup or veto (return false to keep worker running)
        return true;
      },
      onAfterStop: () => {
        console.log('Worker stopped cleanly from top bar');
      },
    },
    onPairingUri: (uri) => {
      // Optional: display an interactive "Approve Pairing in JetPack" button or link
      console.log('Approve pairing URI:', uri);
    },
    onProgress: (progress) => {
      console.log(
        `[${progress.stage ?? 'pull'}] ${progress.percent ?? 0}% - ${progress.message ?? ''}`
      );
    },
  });

  console.log('Worker ready:', client.getAppId());
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof JetPackClientError) {
    if (err.code === 'DAEMON_NOT_RUNNING') {
      console.error(`Install or start JetPack Desktop: ${err.downloadUrl}`);
    } else {
      console.error(`JetPack error [${err.code}]: ${err.message}`);
    }
  } else {
    throw err;
  }
}
```

### What `connectAndEnsureApp()` Automates

1. **Loopback Liveness & Cold-Visit Probe (`GET /health`)**: Probes `http://127.0.0.1:<daemonPort>/health` (bounded by `healthProbeTimeoutMs = 2000` by default). If `jetpack-daemon` is not installed or not running, `connectAndEnsureApp()` rejects immediately with `JetPackClientError('DAEMON_NOT_RUNNING', ..., { downloadUrl })` **without** triggering an unhandled `jetpack://pair` deep link, and updates `JetPackControlBar` to `'Error'` with a sanitized HTTPS **"Download JetPack"** link.
2. **WASM Initialization & Identity**: Loads `jetpack-wasm` and restores (or creates) `WasmClientIdentity` (`Ed25519` + `X25519` keys persisted in `localStorage`).
3. **Auto-Pairing (`autoPair: true`) & WebSocket Session**: If `/health` reports `origin_paired: false` (with W3C Private Network Access headers) or the initial `ClientHello` fails because the origin is unpaired, generates `jetpack://pair?client_id=...&pubkey=...&origin=...`, invokes `onPairingUri(uri)`, triggers the deep link (unless `disableAutoDeepLink: true`), and polls until approved or `pairingTimeoutMs` (`60000ms` default) elapses, then completes the encrypted `X25519` / `Ed25519` handshake on `ws://127.0.0.1:9470`.
4. **Install & Provision Check**: Queries `list_apps()`. If `appId` is missing, resolves `ociReference` from options or `get_catalog()` (verified `SignedAppCatalog`) and runs `pull_app()`, forwarding download, extraction, and environment stages (`oci_layer`, `runtime_download`, `runtime_extract`, `uv_bootstrap`, `python_standalone`, `uv_sync`) to `onProgress` (`percent` is `number | null`).
5. **Worker Boot**: Calls `launch_app(appId, resetVolumes, onProgress)` if the worker is not already `Running` (or attaches this WebSocket session to the running worker), forwarding any just-in-time `runtime_*` / `uv_*` / `sandbox_launch` `app.launch.progress` updates to `onProgress`.
6. **SDK Top Control Bar (`JetPackControlBar`)**: In browser environments (unless `controlBar: false`), automatically mounts an isolated Shadow-DOM top bar displaying the JetPack logo, app name, live status pill (`Connecting`, `Running`, `Stopped`, `Error`), `"Control Center"` link, optional `"Download JetPack"` link (on `DAEMON_NOT_RUNNING`), and `"Stop"` action.

## 2. Send Correlated Zero-Copy Binary Requests (`request`)

Send structured metadata (encoded as MsgPack by `jetpack-wasm`) alongside a zero-copy `Uint8Array` payload directly to your ensured worker:

```typescript
const fileBytes = new Uint8Array(await selectedFile.arrayBuffer());

const response = await client.request(
  'media.inspect',
  { filename: selectedFile.name, include_streams: true },
  fileBytes,
  { timeoutMs: 30_000 }
);

console.log('Reply opcode:', response.opcode);
console.log('Correlation ID:', response.correlationId);
const jsonSummary = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(response.payload));
console.log('Probe result:', jsonSummary);
```

Under the hood, `request()` assigns a monotonic `correlation_id`, encrypts the `HybridFrame` with `ChaCha20-Poly1305`, and resolves once the worker replies with the matching `correlation_id` (or rejects on `app.error` / `system.error` / `REQUEST_TIMEOUT`). Launched workers stay running until explicitly stopped by the user or daemon/session teardown; if the worker is stopped externally (for example from Control Center or the system tray) or exits (`"app.worker.stopped"`), `JetPackControlBar` switches to `'Stopped'` with a `"Relaunch"` button and `request()` transparently wakes the worker via `ensureWorkerRunning()` on your next action.

## 3. Subscribe to Streaming Events (`onStream`) & Clean Up (`close` / `destroy`)

Subscribe to real-time progress frames, telemetry, or unsolicited worker streams by exact opcode or wildcard `'*'`:

```typescript
const unsubscribeProgress = client.onStream('media.transcode.progress', (payload, ctx) => {
  const text = new TextDecoder().decode(payload);
  console.log(`Progress (corr=${ctx.correlationId}):`, text);
});

const unsubscribeAll = client.onStream('*', (payload, ctx) => {
  console.debug(`[stream:${ctx.opcode}] ${payload.byteLength} bytes`);
});

// Trigger a long-running transcode request
const result = await client.request(
  'media.transcode',
  { preset: 'hevc_videotoolbox', crf: 24 },
  new Uint8Array(0)
);

// Clean up when unmounting your UI component
unsubscribeProgress();
unsubscribeAll();
client.close();
// Or call client.destroy() to close the session AND unmount JetPackControlBar
```

`client.close()` shuts down the WebSocket, clears all `onStream` handlers, rejects any pending `request()` promises with `JetPackClientError('CLIENT_CLOSED', ...)`, and transitions `JetPackControlBar` to `'Stopped'`.

## 4. Safe Worker Stop, Standalone `/apps/<app-id>/`, and External `https://` Hosting

`JetPackControlBar` uses `attachShadow({ mode: 'open' })` so host CSS never leaks into the bar or confirmation modal, and Control Bar styles never affect your application:

* **Confirmation Guard**: Clicking **Stop** opens an in-Shadow-DOM confirmation dialog whenever `warnOnUnsavedWork` evaluates to `true` (boolean or predicate callback) or `onBeforeStop` is provided (and `warnOnUnsavedWork` is not `false`).
* **Programmatic Stop**: Call `await client.stopApp()` to send `app.terminate` (`terminate_app(appId)`) without tearing down the bar, keeping it visible with status `'Stopped'`.
* **Standalone MPA/SPA Routes, Dynamic `ui/` Bundles & Window Downloads**: App frontends served by `jetpack-daemon` live under `/apps/<app-id>/` (`http://127.0.0.1:9470/apps/<app-id>/`). When an installed package ships its own `ui/` folder (`<root>/apps/<app-id>/<active_version>/ui/`), `jetpack-daemon` serves that decoupled bundle directly (with canonical boundary checks, MPA `<subpath>/index.html`, and extensionless SPA fallback) before falling back to embedded Control Center assets. By default (`open_in_app_window = true`), Control Center uses `client.open_url(...)` (`"ui.open_url"`) so `jetpack-daemon` opens each app (`/apps/<app-id>/`) and Control Center in its own OS-native `wry` WebView desktop window (`WKWebView` on macOS, `WebView2` on Windows, `WebKitGTK` on Linux) sharing persistent storage in `<root>/webview-data` and supporting both standard HTTP file downloads (into the user's `Downloads` directory) and `blob:` / `data:` `<a download>` exports via a native `rfd` save-file dialog (with transparent default-browser fallback when running headless, or browser tabs when `"Open Dashboard & Apps in Standalone Windows"` is turned off in **My Hardware & Security**), while `jetpack-daemon` multiplexes HTTP static serving, cross-session worker attachment, and reference-counted cleanup on `127.0.0.1:9470`.
* **External `https://` Domains & `CatalogAppEntry.launch_url`**: Third-party web frontends hosted on developer domains (e.g., Vercel, Cloudflare Pages, or a custom `https://` site) connect seamlessly to `http://127.0.0.1:9470/health` and `ws://127.0.0.1:9470` thanks to W3C Private Network Access (`Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network: true`) and canonical `Origin` normalization in `paired_clients.db`. When an `Ed25519`-signed `SignedAppCatalog` entry specifies `launch_url` (an `https://` URL—or loopback `http://` for local development—whose normalized origin is listed in `allowed_origins`), Control Center, the system tray **Launch / Open** menu, and `ui.open_url` open that external URL directly in a dedicated OS-native `wry` window (`WKWebView` with `NSAllowsLocalNetworking` on macOS, `WebView2` on Windows, `WebKitGTK` on Linux) or default browser tab instead of `/apps/<app-id>/`. Both navigation and `window.open` handlers inside `wry` intercept `jetpack://pair` deep links cleanly without error pages.

## 5. Developer Mode Live Log Terminal (`JetPackLogTerminal`)

When Developer Mode is enabled on the local daemon (`developer_mode === true`), `connectAndEnsureApp()` automatically checks `get_settings()`, subscribes via `logs.subscribe`, and mounts an isolated Shadow-DOM bottom drawer (`JetPackLogTerminal`) alongside `JetPackControlBar`:

* **Hidden by default in Standard Mode**: If `developer_mode === false`, the terminal remains unmounted/hidden and never subscribes to `logs.subscribe` (daemon also enforces `DEV_MODE_REQUIRED`).
* **Collapsed Bar + Unread Badge**: Starts collapsed into a slim bottom bar displaying an unread `WARN`/`ERROR` counter badge.
* **Expanded Controls**: Clicking the bar expands live logs with auto-scroll, severity coloring (`INFO`, `WARN`, `ERROR`, `DEBUG`, `TRACE`), source filters (`All`, `Daemon`, `Worker`), `"Clear"`, and `"Copy Logs"` (`"Copied!"` feedback).
* **Opt-out or Custom Config**: Pass `logTerminal: false` to disable auto-mounting or `logTerminal: { title: 'My Worker Logs', maxEntries: 500 }` to customize options, or stream manually via `client.subscribeLogs(entry => ...)` / `client.unsubscribeLogs()`.

## Next Steps

* Inspect all TypeScript interfaces, `JetPackControlBar`, `JetPackLogTerminal`, and low-level `jetpack-wasm` bindings in the [Frontend API Reference](/sdk/frontend/api-reference).
* Review the exact wire layout in the [Binary Framing Protocol](/sdk/frontend/binary-framing).
