# Frontend API Reference

This page documents both the high-level TypeScript SDK (`@jetpack/client`) and the bundled `wasm-bindgen` bindings (`jetpack-wasm`, re-exported via `@jetpack/client/wasm`).

```bash
npm install @jetpack/client
```

## High-Level SDK: `JetPackAppClient<TOpcodes>` (`@jetpack/client`)

Source: `web/packages/jetpack-client/src/client.ts` and `types.ts`. By default, `JetPackAppClient` loads the bundled `@jetpack/client/wasm` module with zero configuration (`wasmModule`, `wasmModulePath`, and `wasmBinaryOrUrl` remain available as optional overrides).

Pass a `JetPackOpcodeMap` interface generated by [`jetpack codegen`](/publishing/cli-tools#jetpack-codegen---worker-path---out-path---strict) (`new JetPackAppClient<JetPackOpcodeMap>()`) for compile-time validation of opcodes, metadata shapes, required `Uint8Array` payloads, response types, and `onStream()` listeners. Omitting the generic (`new JetPackAppClient()`) falls back to `DefaultOpcodeMap` and stays 100% backwards-compatible.

### Methods

| Method | Signature | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `connectAndEnsureApp` | `(options: ConnectAndEnsureAppOptions) => Promise<this>` | Initializes WASM, connects & pairs if needed, pulls from `SignedAppCatalog` if absent, launches or attaches to the worker, mounts `JetPackControlBar`, and mounts/subscribes `JetPackLogTerminal` when `developer_mode === true`. |
| `ensureWorkerRunning` | `() => Promise<void>` | Ensures the sandboxed worker is running, relaunching it via `launch_app` if it was stopped externally (for example via Control Center or manual Stop). Concurrent callers share a single launch operation. |
| `stopApp` | `() => Promise<unknown>` | Terminates the active worker via `terminate_app(appId)`, rejects in-flight requests with `NOT_CONNECTED`, and sets `JetPackControlBar` status to `'Stopped'`. |
| `request` | `<K extends keyof TOpcodes & string>(opcode: K, ...args: OpcodeRequestArgs<TOpcodes, K>) => Promise<WorkerResponse<OpcodeResponseFor<TOpcodes, K>>>` | Sends a correlated `HybridFrame` (`target_worker = appId`) with zero-copy `Uint8Array` transfer and resolves with `{ opcode, payload, correlationId }`. Automatically wakes a stopped worker via `ensureWorkerRunning()` (and retries once on a no-active-worker `system.error` race) while respecting `timeoutMs`. |
| `onStream` | `<K extends (keyof TOpcodes & string) \| '*'>(opcode: K, callback: StreamCallback<K extends '*' ? string : K, OpcodeStreamPayloadFor<TOpcodes, K>>) => () => void` | Subscribes to unsolicited or streaming worker frames matching `opcode` (or `'*'`). Returns an idempotent unsubscribe function. |
| `onWorkerStopped` | `(callback: (event: AppWorkerStoppedEvent) => void) => () => void` | Subscribes to daemon `"app.worker.stopped"` events (`'idle_timeout'`, `'terminated'`, `'process_exited'`). Returns an idempotent unsubscribe function. |
| `onWorkerStarted` | `(callback: (event: { app_id: string }) => void) => () => void` | Subscribes to worker wake/relaunch events emitted after `ensureWorkerRunning()` succeeds. Returns an idempotent unsubscribe function. |
| `subscribeLogs` | `(onEntry: (entry: LogEntry) => void) => Promise<LogsSubscribeOkResponse>` | Subscribes to live sanitized daemon & worker `logs.entry` frames (`logs.subscribe`). Rejects with `DEV_MODE_REQUIRED` when Developer Mode is off. |
| `unsubscribeLogs` | `() => Promise<void>` | Unsubscribes from live log streaming (`logs.unsubscribe`). Safe to call repeatedly. |
| `isConnected` | `() => boolean` | Returns `true` when an authenticated session is active and bound to an ensured `appId`. |
| `isWorkerRunning` | `() => boolean` | Returns `true` when the session is connected and the app worker is currently active. |
| `getLastStopReason` | `() => WorkerStopReason \| null` | Returns the most recent `WorkerStopReason` (`'idle_timeout'`, `'terminated'`, `'process_exited'`) if stopped, or `null` while running. |
| `getAppId` | `() => string \| null` | Returns the currently ensured `appId`, or `null` if disconnected. |
| `getIdentity` | `() => WasmIdentityLike \| null` | Returns the active `WasmClientIdentity`, if initialized. |
| `getLastPairingUri` | `() => string \| null` | Returns the last generated `jetpack://pair?...` URI if auto-pairing ran. |
| `getRawClient` | `() => WasmClientLike \| null` | Exposes the underlying `JetPackWasmClient` for control-plane calls (`get_hardware_profile`, `reset_app_volumes`, etc.). |
| `getControlBar` | `() => JetPackControlBar \| null` | Returns the auto-mounted `JetPackControlBar` instance, or `null` when disabled (`controlBar: false`) or running headless. |
| `getLogTerminal` | `() => JetPackLogTerminal \| null` | Returns the auto-mounted Developer Mode `JetPackLogTerminal` instance, or `null` when Developer Mode is off, disabled (`logTerminal: false`), or running headless. |
| `close` | `() => void` | Closes the WebSocket, unsubscribes live log streams, clears stream/lifecycle listeners, rejects pending `request()` calls with `CLIENT_CLOSED`, hides `JetPackLogTerminal`, and marks `JetPackControlBar` as `'Stopped'`. |
| `destroy` | `() => void` | Calls `close()` and unmounts any auto-mounted `JetPackControlBar` and `JetPackLogTerminal`. |

### `ConnectAndEnsureAppOptions`

```typescript
export interface ConnectAndEnsureAppOptions {
  appId: string;
  daemonPort?: number;              // Default: 9470
  wsUrl?: string;                   // Overrides ws://127.0.0.1:<daemonPort>
  origin?: string;                  // Overrides window.location.origin
  ociReference?: string;            // Explicit OCI ref (for local/custom testing)
  autoPair?: boolean;               // Default: true
  resetVolumes?: boolean;           // Default: false
  pairingPollIntervalMs?: number;   // Default: 1500
  pairingTimeoutMs?: number;        // Default: 60000
  disableAutoDeepLink?: boolean;    // Default: false
  downloadUrl?: string;             // HTTPS download link surfaced on DAEMON_NOT_RUNNING
  healthProbeTimeoutMs?: number;    // /health pre-flight timeout in ms (default: 2000; 0 skips probe)
  fetchFn?: typeof fetch;           // Custom fetch implementation for /health probe (testing/SSR)
  onProgress?: (progress: AppPullProgress) => void;
  onPairingUri?: (uri: string) => void;
  wasmModule?: WasmBindingsAdapter;
  wasmModulePath?: string;
  wasmBinaryOrUrl?: unknown;
  controlBar?: boolean | JetPackControlBarOptions; // Default: auto-mounted in DOM
  logTerminal?: boolean | JetPackLogTerminalOptions; // Auto-mounted only if developer_mode === true
}
```

### `JetPackControlBar` & `JetPackControlBarOptions`

Source: `web/packages/jetpack-client/src/control-bar.ts`. Uses `attachShadow({ mode: 'open' })` for CSS isolation and safely no-ops in headless/SSR environments where `document` is undefined.

```typescript
export type ControlBarWorkerStatus = 'Connecting' | 'Running' | 'Stopped' | 'Error';
export type WorkerStopReason = 'idle_timeout' | 'terminated' | 'process_exited';

export interface AppWorkerStoppedEvent {
  app_id: string;
  job_id: string;
  reason: WorkerStopReason;
}

export interface JetPackControlBarOptions {
  appId?: string;
  appName?: string;
  controlCenterUrl?: string;           // Default: http://127.0.0.1:<daemonPort>/#apps
  downloadUrl?: string;                // Optional HTTPS download link for Error state
  logoUrl?: string;                    // Overrides built-in JetPack SVG icon
  mountTarget?: HTMLElement | null;    // Default: document.body; pass null to defer mount()
  initialStatus?: ControlBarWorkerStatus; // Default: 'Connecting'
  onBeforeStop?: () => Promise<boolean> | boolean;
  warnOnUnsavedWork?: boolean | (() => boolean);
  stopConfirmTitle?: string;
  stopConfirmMessage?: string;
  onStop?: () => Promise<unknown>;     // Wired automatically to client.stopApp()
  onRelaunch?: () => Promise<unknown>; // Wired automatically to client.ensureWorkerRunning()
  onAfterStop?: () => Promise<void> | void;
  onStopError?: (error: Error) => void;
}
```

| Method | Signature | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `mount` | `(target?: HTMLElement \| null) => boolean` | Inserts `#jetpack-control-bar-host` at the top of `target` (or `document.body`). Returns `false` if headless. |
| `unmount` | `() => void` | Removes the host element and clears modal/keyboard listeners. |
| `updateOptions` | `(partial: Partial<JetPackControlBarOptions>) => void` | Updates bar options live and refreshes rendered text/links. |
| `setStatus` | `(status: ControlBarWorkerStatus, detail?: string, options?: { downloadUrl?: string }) => void` | Updates the live status pill, optional `'Stopped'` status note or `'Error'` detail tooltip, and renders a sanitized `https://` `"Download JetPack"` link when in `'Error'` state (non-HTTPS URLs are ignored). |
| `getStatus` | `() => ControlBarWorkerStatus` | Returns the current status (`'Connecting'`, `'Running'`, `'Stopped'`, or `'Error'`). |
| `setAppName` / `setControlCenterUrl` | `(value: string) => void` | Updates the displayed app name or `"Control Center"` destination URL. |
| `triggerRelaunch` | `() => Promise<boolean>` | Invokes `onRelaunch()` when `status === 'Stopped'` and transitions the bar back to `'Running'` on success. |
| `triggerStop` | `() => Promise<boolean>` | Opens the Shadow-DOM confirmation modal when `warnOnUnsavedWork` evaluates to `true` or `onBeforeStop` is set (unless `warnOnUnsavedWork === false`); otherwise stops directly. |
| `confirmStopModal` / `cancelStopModal` | `() => Promise<boolean>` / `() => void` | Confirms (running `onBeforeStop` -> `onStop` -> `onAfterStop`) or dismisses the modal. |
| `isModalOpen` | `() => boolean` | Returns `true` when the stop confirmation modal is currently visible. |
| `getHostElement` / `getShadowRoot` | `() => HTMLElement \| null` / `() => ShadowRoot \| null` | Exposes the mounted host element and open `ShadowRoot`. |

### `JetPackLogTerminal` & Log Streaming Types

Source: `web/packages/jetpack-client/src/log-terminal.ts` and `types.ts`. Uses `attachShadow({ mode: 'open' })` for CSS isolation and renders strictly when `developerMode` is `true` (collapsing into a thin bottom bar with an unread `WARN`/`ERROR` counter by default).

```typescript
export type LogLevel = 'INFO' | 'WARN' | 'ERROR' | 'DEBUG' | 'TRACE' | string;
export type LogSourceFilter = 'all' | 'daemon' | 'worker';

export interface LogEntry {
  timestamp_ms: number;
  level: LogLevel;
  source: string; // "daemon" or app_id (e.g. "io.jetpack.media-converter")
  message: string;
}

export interface LogsSubscribeOkResponse {
  buffered_count: number;
}

export interface JetPackLogTerminalOptions {
  mountTarget?: HTMLElement | null; // Default: document.body; pass null to defer mount()
  developerMode?: boolean;          // Default: false (hidden unless true)
  maxEntries?: number;              // Default: 1000 buffered rows
  title?: string;                   // Default: 'JetPack Live Logs'
  expanded?: boolean;               // Default: false (thin collapsed header bar)
  sourceFilter?: LogSourceFilter;   // Default: 'all'
  copyToClipboard?: (text: string) => Promise<void>;
  onCopySuccess?: (text: string) => void;
  onCopyError?: (error: Error) => void;
}
```

| Method | Signature | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `mount` / `unmount` | `(target?: HTMLElement \| null) => boolean` / `() => void` | Attaches or removes `#jetpack-log-terminal-host` on `target` (`document.body` by default). |
| `setDeveloperMode` / `isDeveloperMode` | `(enabled: boolean) => void` / `() => boolean` | Shows or hides the bottom drawer strictly according to `developerMode` (collapses when disabled). |
| `setExpanded` / `toggle` / `isExpanded` | `(expanded: boolean) => void` / `() => void` / `() => boolean` | Expands or collapses the drawer body, resetting unread `WARN`/`ERROR` count and auto-scrolling on expand. |
| `setSourceFilter` / `getSourceFilter` | `(filter: LogSourceFilter) => void` / `() => LogSourceFilter` | Filters displayed rows between `'all'`, `'daemon'`, and `'worker'`. |
| `appendEntry` / `clear` | `(entry: LogEntry) => void` / `() => void` | Appends a log row (incrementing unread `WARN`/`ERROR` count while collapsed) or clears buffered logs. |
| `getUnreadWarningErrorCount` / `getEntries` / `getVisibleEntries` | `() => number` / `() => LogEntry[]` / `() => LogEntry[]` | Inspects unread alert count, full buffer, or currently filtered log entries. |
| `formatAllLogsText` / `copyLogs` | `() => string` / `() => Promise<boolean>` | Formats all buffered logs and copies them to clipboard, showing `"Copied!"` button confirmation. |
| `updateOptions` | `(partial: Partial<JetPackLogTerminalOptions>) => void` | Updates options live without clearing buffered entries. |
| `getHostElement` / `getShadowRoot` | `() => HTMLElement \| null` / `() => ShadowRoot \| null` | Exposes the mounted host element and open `ShadowRoot`. |

### `JetPackOpcodeMap`, `WorkerResponse` & `StreamCallback`

```typescript
export interface JetPackOpcodeEntry<
  TMeta = Record<string, unknown> | null,
  TResponse = unknown,
  TBinary extends boolean = boolean,
  TStream extends boolean = boolean,
> {
  meta: TMeta;
  response: TResponse;
  binary?: TBinary;
  stream?: TStream;
}

export type JetPackOpcodeMap = Record<string, JetPackOpcodeEntry<any, any, boolean, boolean>>;

export interface DefaultOpcodeMap {
  [opcode: string]: JetPackOpcodeEntry<Record<string, unknown> | null, unknown, boolean, boolean>;
}

export interface WorkerResponse<TResponse = unknown> {
  opcode: string;
  payload: Uint8Array;
  correlationId: number;
  readonly __responseType?: TResponse;
}

export interface StreamFrameContext<TOpcode extends string = string, TPayload = unknown> {
  opcode: TOpcode;
  correlationId: number | null;
  readonly __payloadType?: TPayload;
}

export type StreamCallback<TOpcode extends string = string, TPayload = unknown> = (
  payload: Uint8Array,
  context: StreamFrameContext<TOpcode, TPayload>
) => void;
```

### `JetPackClientError` & Codes

`JetPackClientError` exposes `readonly code: JetPackClientErrorCode` and `readonly downloadUrl?: string` (populated on `DAEMON_NOT_RUNNING`, defaulting to `DEFAULT_JETPACK_DOWNLOAD_URL = 'https://github.com/jetpack-desktop/releases/releases/latest'`).

| Code | Cause |
| :--- | :--- |
| `DAEMON_NOT_RUNNING` | `GET /health` timed out, failed to connect, or returned non-OK before pairing/WebSocket handshake. `err.downloadUrl` contains the sanitized `https://` JetPack installer link. |
| `NOT_CONNECTED` | `request()` or `stopApp()` called before `connectAndEnsureApp()` succeeded. |
| `CLIENT_CLOSED` | `request()` or `stopApp()` called after `close()`, or `close()` invoked while a request was in flight. |
| `PAIRING_TIMEOUT` | User did not approve `jetpack://pair` within `pairingTimeoutMs`. |
| `APP_NOT_IN_CATALOG` | `appId` is neither installed locally nor present in `SignedAppCatalog` (and `ociReference` was omitted). |
| `REQUEST_TIMEOUT` | Worker did not reply within `RequestOptions.timeoutMs`. |
| `WASM_LOAD_FAILED` | Failed to dynamically import `jetpack-wasm` bindings. |
| `INVALID_OPTIONS` | Missing or empty `appId` passed to `connectAndEnsureApp()`. |

***

## Low-Level WASM Bindings (`@jetpack/client/wasm` / `jetpack-wasm`)

Source: `crates/jetpack-wasm/src/identity.rs` and `client.rs` (bundled inside `@jetpack/client` under `@jetpack/client/wasm`).

```typescript
import initWasm, { WasmClientIdentity, JetPackWasmClient } from '@jetpack/client/wasm';

await initWasm();
```

### `WasmClientIdentity`

* `new WasmClientIdentity()` (`load_or_generate`): Loads or generates `client_id` (`UUIDv4`) + `Ed25519` / `X25519` 32-byte seeds in `localStorage` (`jetpack_client_id`, `jetpack_ed25519_seed`, `jetpack_x25519_seed`), falling back to ephemeral in-memory keys if storage is blocked.
* `WasmClientIdentity.generate_new_ephemeral()`: Creates a fresh in-memory identity without touching `localStorage`.
* `WasmClientIdentity.clear_storage()`: Removes persisted identity keys from `localStorage`.
* `identity.client_id`: Getter returning the `UUIDv4` string.
* `identity.public_key_bundle_base64()`: Returns the URL-safe Base64 64-byte (`Ed25519` + `X25519`) public key bundle.
* `identity.ed25519_pubkey_hex()` / `identity.x25519_pubkey_hex()`: Returns 32-byte hex public keys.
* `identity.generate_pairing_uri(origin)`: Validates and normalizes `origin` and returns `jetpack://pair?client_id=...&pubkey=...&origin=...`.

### `JetPackWasmClient`

| Method | Return Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `JetPackWasmClient.connect(wsUrl, identity, origin?)` | `Promise<JetPackWasmClient>` | Opens binary WebSocket (`arraybuffer`) and executes `ClientHello` / `ServerHello` handshake. |
| `is_connected()` | `boolean` | Returns `true` when in `Established` encrypted session state. |
| `get_hardware_profile()` | `Promise<HardwareProfile>` | Sends `hardware.get_profile` and resolves with CPU, RAM/unified memory, and GPU device details. |
| `get_catalog()` | `Promise<CatalogAppEntry[]>` | Fetches verified entries from the active `SignedAppCatalog` (refreshed via `catalog_url` with cached/embedded fallback), including `coming_soon?: boolean`, `launch_url?: string \| null`, and `poster_url?: string \| null`. |
| `list_apps()` | `Promise<AppInfo[]>` | Lists installed apps with `status`, `is_verified`, and sanitized `volumes` (`folder_name`, `is_configured`—never host paths). |
| `pull_app(imageRef, onProgress?, appId?)` | `Promise<AppPullOkResponse>` | Pulls a catalog-verified OCI app and streams `app.pull.progress` events (`percent` may be `number \| null`). |
| `launch_app(appId, resetVolumes?, onProgress?)` | `Promise<AppLaunchOkResponse>` | Starts sandboxed worker (`resetVolumes` forces fresh `rfd` folder prompts). Optional `onProgress` receives `app.launch.progress` events (`runtime_download`, `runtime_extract`, `uv_bootstrap`, `python_standalone`, `uv_sync`, `sandbox_launch`) while remaining compatible with 1- and 2-argument calls. |
| `reset_app_volumes(appId, volumeName?)` | `Promise<AppVolumesResetOkResponse>` | Clears persisted `authorized_volumes` entries in `paired_clients.db`. |
| `clear_app_cache(appId)` | `Promise<AppClearCacheOkResponse>` | Loopback Control-Center-only (`127.0.0.1` / `localhost`, rejecting non-Control-Center origins with `APP_MANAGEMENT_ORIGIN_FORBIDDEN` and active workers with `APP_IS_RUNNING`). Removes `<appdata_root>/<app_id>`, recreates an empty `0o700` directory on Unix, and clears `authorized_volumes` rows without touching mounted host folders or application bundles. |
| `uninstall_app(appId, removeCache?)` | `Promise<AppUninstallOkResponse>` | Loopback Control-Center-only (`APP_MANAGEMENT_ORIGIN_FORBIDDEN` / `APP_IS_RUNNING`). Removes all installed bundle directories for `appId` under `<apps_dir>`, and when `removeCache` is `true`, also removes `<appdata_root>/<app_id>` and clears `authorized_volumes` rows. Never deletes mounted host folders, `.core-apps-seeded`, shared blobs, or shared runtimes. |
| `terminate_app(appIdOrJobId)` | `Promise<AppTerminateOkResponse>` | Terminates a running job and its OS sandbox. |
| `list_paired_clients()` | `Promise<PairedClientSummary[]>` | Lists paired browser clients from `paired_clients.db`. |
| `revoke_client(clientId?, origin?)` | `Promise<ClientRevokeOkResponse>` | Revokes paired client access. |
| `get_settings()` / `set_developer_mode(enabled)` / `set_open_in_app_window(enabled)` / `set_open_dashboard_on_startup(enabled)` | `Promise<DaemonSettings>` | Reads or partially updates daemon UI settings (`developer_mode`, `open_in_app_window`, `open_dashboard_on_startup`, `daemon_version`, `appdata_dir`). |
| `pick_appdata_dir()` / `reset_appdata_dir()` | `Promise<DaemonSettings>` | Loopback-only (`127.0.0.1` / `localhost`). `pick_appdata_dir()` opens the daemon's main-thread OS folder picker (`rfd`) to choose a custom `appdata_dir` root (rejects with `APPDATA_PICKER_CANCELLED` on cancel); `reset_appdata_dir()` restores `<root>/appdata`. |
| `subscribe_logs(onEntryCallback)` | `Promise<LogsSubscribeOkResponse>` | Sends `logs.subscribe` and streams sanitized `logs.entry` (`{ timestamp_ms, level, source, message }`) frames; rejects with `DEV_MODE_REQUIRED` if Developer Mode is off. |
| `unsubscribe_logs()` | `Promise<LogsUnsubscribeOkResponse>` | Sends `logs.unsubscribe` and clears the active log callback. |
| `open_url(url)` | `Promise<UiOpenUrlOkResponse>` | Loopback-only caller (`127.0.0.1` / `localhost`). Opens either a validated loopback HTTP URL or an exact `launch_url` declared in the active Ed25519-verified `SignedAppCatalog` (with origin in `allowed_origins`) in a dedicated OS-native `wry` WebView window (`WKWebView` with `NSAllowsLocalNetworking` / `WebView2` / `WebKitGTK`, persisted under `<root>/webview-data` and intercepting `jetpack://pair` deep links) when `open_in_app_window` is `true` (with headless default-browser fallback) or a browser tab when `false`, resolving to `{ opened_in_app_window }`. |
| `export_diagnostics()` | `Promise<DiagnosticsExportResult>` | Requests `diagnostics.export` and returns `{ filename, generated_at_unix, log_tail_bytes, log_truncated, redactions_applied, zip_bytes }` where `zip_bytes` is a `Uint8Array` sliced from the binary frame. |
| `send_diagnostics()` | `Promise<DiagnosticsSendOkResponse>` | Requests `diagnostics.send` to transmit a sanitized diagnostic JSON report to `[diagnostics].report_url` (rejects with `[DIAGNOSTICS_DISABLED]` when `report_url` is unset). |
| `check_for_updates()` | `Promise<UpdateStatusResponse>` | Sends `update.check` and resolves with `{ current_version, latest_version, update_available, release_url, asset_name, checked_at_secs, error }`. |
| `apply_update(onProgress?, expectedVersion?)` | `Promise<UpdateRestartingResponse>` | Control-Center-only (`127.0.0.1` own origin). Sends `update.apply`, streams `UpdateProgressFrame` (`checking`, `downloading`, `verifying`, `extracting`, `installing`, `restarting`, `percent`, `bytes_downloaded`, `total_bytes`, `message`) to `onProgress`, and resolves with `{ target_version, restart_delay_ms }` before daemon restart. |
| `send_worker_frame(targetWorker, opcode, metaJs, rawPayload)` | `void` | Fire-and-forget encrypted `HybridFrame` dispatch to a worker. |
| `request_worker_frame(targetWorker, opcode, metaJs, rawPayload)` | `Promise<WorkerResponse>` | Correlated worker request matching `correlation_id`. |
| `on_worker_frame(callback)` | `void` | Registers `(opcode, payloadUint8Array, correlationId)` listener for unsolicited/stream frames. |
| `on_worker_stopped(callback)` | `void` | Registers `(event)` listener invoked when the daemon pushes `"app.worker.stopped"` (`{ app_id, job_id, reason }`). |
| `close()` | `void` | Closes WebSocket, clears log/worker listeners, and fails pending promises. |

---
url: https://jetpack-desktop.github.io/sdk/frontend/binary-framing.md
description: >-
  Hybrid zero-copy binary framing protocol combining compact MsgPack headers
  with raw binary payloads and ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD.
---

# Binary Framing Protocol

JetPack prohibits JSON over WebSockets for control-plane and worker data payloads. Every message uses **Hybrid Binary Framing** (`crates/jetpack-proto/src/framing.rs`) so structured metadata stays compact via MessagePack while large buffers (tensors, audio PCM, video frames, JPEG previews) remain raw zero-copy bytes.

## 1. Plaintext Hybrid Frame Layout

```text
+-------------------------------+------------------------+------------------------+
| header_len: uint32 LE (4 B)   | MsgPack Header (N B)   | Raw Binary Payload (M) |
+-------------------------------+------------------------+------------------------+
|<--------- 4 bytes ----------->|<------ N bytes ------->|<------ M bytes ------->|
```

* **Size Limits**:
  * `MAX_HEADER_SIZE`: `64 KiB` (`65,536` bytes)
  * `MAX_FRAME_SIZE`: `64 MiB` (`67,108,864` bytes)
* **Zero-Copy Slicing**: On decode, `jetpack-proto` validates `plaintext.len() >= 4 + N`, deserializes the MsgPack header from `&plaintext[4 .. 4 + N]`, and returns `Bytes::slice(4 + N ..)` as the payload without allocating or copying the `M`-byte binary body.

### `FrameHeader` Schema (MsgPack Map)

Serialized with named MsgPack fields (`rmp_serde::to_vec_named`):

```rust
pub struct FrameHeader {
    pub channel_id: u32,
    pub opcode: String,
    pub correlation_id: Option<u64>,
    pub target_worker: Option<String>,
}
```

| Field | Type | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `channel_id` | `u32` | Logical multiplexing stream/channel (`0` for control plane, `1+` for worker channels). |
| `opcode` | `string` | Operation identifier (e.g. `"hardware.get_profile"`, `"app.launch"`, `"compute.tensor_op"`). |
| `correlation_id` | `u64?` | Optional request/response correlation ID matched by `JetPackAppClient.request()`. |
| `target_worker` | `string?` | `None` routes to the daemon control plane; `Some(app_id)` or `Some("primary")` routes to the primary worker; `Some(service_name)` routes to a `[services.<name>]` companion. |

## 2. Encrypted WebSocket Wire Envelope

Over `ws://127.0.0.1:9470`, each plaintext `HybridFrame` is authenticated and encrypted using `ChaCha20-Poly1305`:

```text
+-------------------------------+----------------------------------------+------------------------+
| seq: uint64 LE (8 B, AAD)     | Ciphertext of Plaintext Frame (4+N+M)  | Poly1305 Tag (16 B)    |
+-------------------------------+----------------------------------------+------------------------+
```

* **Nonce Construction (`12 B`)**:
  * Client -> Daemon: `b"C2D\0" || seq.to_le_bytes()`
  * Daemon -> Client: `b"D2C\0" || seq.to_le_bytes()`
* **Replay Protection**: Both sides start `seq` at `0` and require `incoming_seq == expected_seq` strictly incrementing by `+1`.
* **Text Frame Rejection**: Any `Message::Text` frame received after handshake completion triggers immediate connection termination with WebSocket close code `1003 Unsupported Data`.

## 3. Local Kernel Worker IPC Framing

Between `jetpack-daemon` and sandboxed workers (`UDS` on macOS/Linux, `Named Pipe` on Windows), traffic crosses an OS-isolated local boundary and is **not** re-encrypted. Instead, stream boundaries are delimited by an outer 4-byte frame length (`sdks/python/jetpack_sdk/framing.py`):

```text
+-------------------------------+-------------------------------+------------------------+------------------------+
| frame_len: uint32 LE (4 B)    | header_len: uint32 LE (4 B)   | MsgPack Header (N B)   | Raw Binary Payload (M) |
+-------------------------------+-------------------------------+------------------------+------------------------+
```

Where `frame_len = 4 + N + M`. This allows Python workers (`memoryview`) and Rust IPC readers (`bytes::Bytes`) to read each frame in two contiguous reads without scanning or base64 decoding.

## 4. Control-Plane Opcodes Summary

| Request Opcode | Response / Stream Opcodes | Payload Direction |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `hardware.get_profile` | `hardware.profile` | Empty -> `HardwareProfile` (MsgPack) |
| `catalog.get` | `catalog.ok` | Empty -> `CatalogAppEntry[]` (MsgPack) |
| `app.list` | `app.list.ok` | Empty -> `AppInfo[]` (MsgPack) |
| `app.pull` | `app.pull.progress`, `app.pull.ok`, `app.error` | `AppPullRequest` -> Progress / OK (updating an existing app rejects `APP_IS_RUNNING` if active, swaps in the new version, cleans superseded version folders under `<apps_dir>/<app_id>/`, and preserves `<appdata_root>/<app_id>` and mounted host folders) |
| `app.launch` | `app.launch.progress`, `app.launch.ok`, `app.error` | `AppLaunchRequest` -> `AppLaunchProgressFrame` (`stage`, `message`, `percent?`, `downloaded_bytes`, `total_bytes`) / `job_id` |
| `app.volumes.reset` | `app.volumes.reset.ok`, `app.error` | `AppVolumesResetRequest` -> `reset_count` |
| `app.cache.clear` | `app.cache.clear.ok`, `app.error` | `AppClearCacheRequest` (`app_id`) -> `AppClearCacheOkResponse` (`app_id`, `cleared_appdata`, `reset_volumes`; Control Center origin only; rejects `APP_IS_RUNNING`) |
| `app.uninstall` | `app.uninstall.ok`, `app.error` | `AppUninstallRequest` (`app_id`, `remove_cache`) -> `AppUninstallOkResponse` (`app_id`, `removed_app_dirs`, `cleared_appdata`, `reset_volumes`; Control Center origin only; rejects `APP_IS_RUNNING`) |
| `app.terminate` | `app.terminate.ok`, `app.error` | `AppTerminateRequest` -> OK |
| `client.list` / `client.revoke` | `client.list.ok` / `client.revoke.ok` | Client management |
| `settings.get` / `settings.set` | `settings.get.ok` / `settings.ok` | `DaemonSettings` (`developer_mode`, `open_in_app_window`, `open_dashboard_on_startup`, `daemon_version`, `appdata_dir`); `settings.set` accepts optional `reset_appdata_dir: bool` (loopback only) |
| `settings.pick_appdata_dir` | `settings.ok`, `app.error` | Loopback-only (`127.0.0.1` / `localhost`). Opens native main-thread OS folder picker (`rfd`), creates and persists `appdata_dir`, and returns updated `DaemonSettings` |
| `ui.open_url` | `ui.open_url.ok`, `app.error` | `UiOpenUrlRequest` -> `UiOpenUrlOkResponse` (loopback origins & loopback HTTP targets only) |
| `update.check` | `update.status`, `app.error` | Empty -> `UpdateStatusResponse` |
| `update.apply` | `update.progress`, `update.restarting`, `app.error` | `UpdateApplyRequest` -> Progress / Restarting (Control Center origin only) |
| `logs.subscribe` | `logs.subscribe.ok`, `logs.entry`, `app.error` | `LogsSubscribeRequest?` -> Replays bounded 200-entry redacted buffer and streams live `LogEntryFrame` (`timestamp_ms`, `level`, `source`, `message`); rejects with `DEV_MODE_REQUIRED` unless `developer_mode == true` and cancels active streams immediately if `settings.set` disables Developer Mode |
| `logs.unsubscribe` | `logs.unsubscribe.ok` | `LogsUnsubscribeRequest?` -> Cancels the session's live log stream |
| `system.echo` | `system.echo` | Diagnostic raw echo |

  Zero-dependency Python Worker SDK (jetpack_sdk), memoryview zero-copy framing,
  optional @opcode contract decorators, and hermetic uv GPU wheel provisioning.

# Python Worker SDK (`jetpack_sdk`) & GPU Wheels

JetPack provides a lightweight, zero-dependency Python SDK (`sdks/python/jetpack_sdk`, published as `jetpack-sdk` on PyPI) for building sandboxed AI, tensor, and media workers, paired with a hermetic `uv` + `python-build-standalone` provisioner inside `jetpack-daemon`.

## Installation

Install `jetpack-sdk` from PyPI for local worker development, testing, or `uv` lockfile generation:

```bash
# Using uv (recommended)
uv add jetpack-sdk

# Or using pip (zero mandatory runtime dependencies)
pip install jetpack-sdk

# Optional C-extension MsgPack acceleration
pip install "jetpack-sdk[msgpack]"
```

* **Zero Mandatory Dependencies**: `jetpack-sdk` works out-of-the-box with zero third-party packages using its built-in pure-Python MsgPack codec (`sdks/python/jetpack_sdk/framing.py`). Installing the optional `msgpack` extra accelerates large header encoding/decoding when desired.
* **Offline Daemon Embedding**: When `jetpack-daemon` provisions `[python_env]` inside an end-user sandbox (`crates/jetpack-daemon/src/python.rs`), it automatically materializes the embedded `jetpack-sdk` wheel/module into `<app_dir>/.venv` offline without requiring PyPI network access.

## 1. Connecting via `JetPackClient`

When `jetpack-daemon` launches your worker inside its OS sandbox, it sets `JETPACK_IPC_ENDPOINT` to the job's Unix Domain Socket (`ipc.sock`) or Windows Named Pipe (`\\.\pipe\jetpack-worker-<job_id>`).

```python
from jetpack_sdk import FrameHeader, HybridFrame, JetPackClient

with JetPackClient() as client:
    while True:
        frame = client.read_frame()
        if frame is None:
            break  # Daemon closed IPC channel; exit cleanly

        header = frame.header
        if header.opcode == "compute.echo":
            # Reply preserving channel_id and correlation_id
            client.send_frame(
                opcode="compute.echo.ok",
                payload=frame.payload,
                channel_id=header.channel_id,
                correlation_id=header.correlation_id,
            )
```

### `JetPackClient` API (`sdks/python/jetpack_sdk/client.py`)

* `JetPackClient(endpoint: Optional[str] = None)`: Connects to `endpoint` or reads `JETPACK_IPC_ENDPOINT`. Supports context manager (`with JetPackClient() as client:`).
* `read_frame(timeout: Optional[float] = None) -> Optional[HybridFrame]`: Reads the next `[4B frame_len] + [4B header_len] + [MsgPack Header] + [Raw Payload]` frame; returns `None` on EOF.
* `send(frame: HybridFrame) -> None`: Serializes and writes a `HybridFrame`.
* `send_frame(opcode, payload=b"", channel_id=0, correlation_id=None, target_worker=None) -> None`: Convenience wrapper constructing `FrameHeader` + `HybridFrame`.
* `app_home -> Path`: Property returning the app's persistent isolated private data directory from `JETPACK_APP_HOME` (`<appdata_root>/<app_id>`), pre-mounted read-write on launch without any `rfd` prompt (raises `RuntimeError` if unset or empty).
* `proxy_endpoint -> Optional[str]`: Property returning `JETPACK_PROXY_ENDPOINT` / `HTTP_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY` when outbound network rules are granted.
* `@opcode(name, *, request=None, response=None, binary=False, stream=False)` (or `@client.opcode(...)`) and `get_opcode_metadata(fn)`: Optional zero-dependency decorator (`sdks/python/jetpack_sdk/decorators.py`) attaching `__jetpack_opcode__` metadata inspected by `jetpack codegen` to generate `JetPackOpcodeMap` TypeScript contracts.

## 2. Zero-Copy `memoryview` Buffer Processing

Avoid intermediate `bytes` copies or JSON encoding when processing tensors, audio chunks, or image frames. Wrap `frame.payload` in Python's `memoryview` (inspired by `examples/gpu-tensor-worker/worker.py`):

```python
import array
import struct
from jetpack_sdk import JetPackClient


def handle_tensor_op(client: JetPackClient, frame) -> None:
    # Zero-copy view over the binary payload bytes
    mv = memoryview(frame.payload)

    # Example binary layout: [uint32 count][float32 * count]
    (count,) = struct.unpack_from("<I", mv, 0)
    floats_view = mv[4 : 4 + count * 4].cast("f")

    # Process in-place into an array/tensor buffer without string conversion
    scaled = array.array("f", (x * 2.0 for x in floats_view))
    out_bytes = memoryview(scaled).tobytes()

    client.send_frame(
        opcode="compute.tensor_result",
        payload=out_bytes,
        channel_id=frame.header.channel_id,
        correlation_id=frame.header.correlation_id,
    )
```

For NumPy or PyTorch workflows, `torch.frombuffer(memoryview(frame.payload), dtype=torch.float32)` maps directly onto the incoming frame buffer with zero copying on CPU before transferring to CUDA or MPS.

## 3. Hermetic `uv` Provisioning & Automatic GPU Wheel Selection

When an `app.toml` declares `[python_env]`, `jetpack-daemon` (`crates/jetpack-daemon/src/python.rs`) provisions `<app_dir>/.venv` **without ever touching host Python** (`/usr/bin/python3`, Homebrew, Conda, or Windows Registry Python):

* `env_clear()` strips inherited `PYTHONPATH`, `PYTHONHOME`, `VIRTUAL_ENV`, and `CONDA_PREFIX`.
* `UV_NO_CONFIG=1` and `UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-managed` restrict `uv` strictly to `<root>/runtimes/uv/` and `<root>/runtimes/python/` (`python-build-standalone`).
* `UV_CACHE_DIR=<root>/cache/uv` (mode `0700`) shares downloaded wheels across all apps using `UV_LINK_MODE=clone` (macOS APFS) or `UV_LINK_MODE=hardlink` (Linux/Windows).
* If `[python_env].uv_lock_sha256` is specified, `<app_dir>/uv.lock` is SHA-256 verified before invoking `uv --locked`.
* While bootstrapping portable `uv` via HTTP, `PythonProvisioner` inspects `reqwest::Response::content_length()` to stream byte-level `uv_bootstrap` progress (`downloaded_bytes`, `total_bytes`, `percent`) and emits `python_standalone` and `uv_sync` stage updates over `app.pull.progress` and `app.launch.progress`.
* Upon completion, `<app_dir>/.venv/.jetpack-provisioned.json` is written so subsequent launches skip redundant provisioning (**Fast Replay**).

### Hardware-Aware Backend Resolution (`PythonComputeBackend`)

Combining `HardwareProfile` (`004-hardware-discovery`), `[hardware].accelerators`, and `[permissions].gpu_access`, the daemon automatically selects the optimal wheel index:

| Host Hardware & Manifest | Selected Backend | Default PyTorch Wheel Index (or `[python_env.backend_indexes]`) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| NVIDIA GPU (`NVML`) + `"cuda"` + `gpu_access = true` | `cuda` | `https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124` |
| Apple Silicon (`Metal`) + `"metal"` / `"mps"` / `"mlx"` + `gpu_access = true` | `mps` | Standard PyPI native `darwin/arm64` wheels |
| AMD GPU + `"rocm"` + `gpu_access = true` | `rocm` | `https://download.pytorch.org/whl/rocm6.2` |
| No matching GPU or `gpu_access = false` | `cpu` | `https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu` |

You can override any backend index per app in `app.toml`:

```toml
[python_env]
python_version = "3.12"
requirements = ["jetpack-sdk", "torch>=2.4.0"]
uv_lock_sha256 = "428843fd0e0da23463920ba9aa0191a39f32a47b02e97a936c974ba996b4b98f"
isolated = true

[python_env.backend_indexes]
cuda = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124"
rocm = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/rocm6.2"
cpu = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu"
```

---
url: https://jetpack-desktop.github.io/sdk/worker/native-runtimes.md
description: >-
  Declare SHA-256 verified portable native runtimes such as FFmpeg and llama.cpp
  in app.toml without polluting host PATH.
---

# Native Portable Runtimes

Workers often depend on heavy native binaries such as `ffmpeg`, `ffprobe`, `llama.cpp`, or `postgres`. Installing them globally violates **Zero System Pollution**. Instead, `jetpack-daemon` provides `RuntimeProvisioner` (`crates/jetpack-daemon/src/worker/runtimes.rs`) and the OCI Content-Addressable Storage (CAS) manager (`crates/jetpack-daemon/src/oci.rs`).

## 1. Declaring Runtimes in `app.toml`

You can declare either an OCI-backed runtime or per-platform portable HTTPS archives with mandatory `sha256` digests. Example from `examples/ffmpeg-media-converter/app.toml`:

```toml
[runtimes.ffmpeg]
version = "9.0.2"
target_dir = "runtimes/ffmpeg-9.0.2"

[runtimes.ffmpeg.platforms."darwin/arm64"]
url = "https://github.com/Tyrrrz/FFmpegBin/releases/download/9.0.2/ffmpeg-osx-arm64.zip"
digest = "sha256:7d22a2893ccd761c3b4214165975e306d6c85c1de188f79f7e2723070c0006e4"

[runtimes.ffmpeg.platforms."linux/amd64"]
url = "https://github.com/Tyrrrz/FFmpegBin/releases/download/9.0.2/ffmpeg-linux-x64.zip"
digest = "sha256:2483332318255c1001facbc6a6bf91941e5f35651bf8b7d4cfd768e1da18567f"

[runtimes.ffmpeg.platforms."windows/amd64"]
url = "https://github.com/Tyrrrz/FFmpegBin/releases/download/9.0.2/ffmpeg-windows-x64.zip"
digest = "sha256:bcc61c7027eefbed7d87af0a619ce8e6c4a5c5f8bb0d31a2acec8fe7ed749850"
```

## 2. Provisioning Pipeline & Security Checks

During `"app.pull"` and right before `launch_job`, `RuntimeProvisioner`:

1. **Checks Cache**: Inspects `<root>/runtimes/<name>-<version>/bin/`. If already materialized, skips network downloads.
2. **Downloads Target Platform Artifact**: Fetches the platform-matching OCI layer or HTTPS archive (`.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, `.zip`) into a temporary staging file while tracking `reqwest::Response::content_length()` and streaming throttled `runtime_download` progress (`downloaded_bytes`, `total_bytes`, determinate `percent` when `Content-Length` is present or `None` for chunked/unknown sizes) over `app.pull.progress` and `app.launch.progress`.
3. **Verifies SHA-256 Digest**: Computes streaming `SHA-256` and compares against the manifest's `sha256:<64-hex>`. Any mismatch deletes the staging file immediately and fails with `JetPackError::DigestMismatch`.
4. **Tar-Slip / Zip-Slip Safe Extraction**: Emits an indeterminate `runtime_extract` stage update, rejects any archive entry containing `..`, absolute paths, or escaping symlinks/hardlinks, and sets `0o755` executable permissions on Unix binaries.
5. **Zero-Duplication Linking**: Links shared runtime trees and app bundles using `std::fs::hard_link` (shared inode / NTFS file record) or `libc::clonefile` (macOS APFS Copy-on-Write clones) so multiple apps share multi-gigabyte weights and tools without duplicating disk blocks.

## 3. Calling Native Binaries Inside the Sandbox

When `jetpack-daemon` launches the sandboxed worker, `<root>/runtimes/<name>-<version>/bin` is prepended to the **worker's** isolated `PATH` (read-only inside the sandbox), while the host OS `PATH` remains completely untouched.

Your worker can invoke `ffmpeg` directly via `subprocess`:

```python
import shutil
import subprocess

ffmpeg_bin = shutil.which("ffmpeg")
if not ffmpeg_bin:
    raise RuntimeError("ffmpeg runtime was not provisioned into sandbox PATH")

# Example: Apple Silicon VideoToolbox or CPU transcode inside sandbox
cmd = [
    ffmpeg_bin,
    "-y",
    "-i", input_path,
    "-c:v", "h264_videotoolbox",
    output_path,
]
subprocess.run(cmd, check=True)
```

For full reference code, see `examples/ffmpeg-media-converter/transcoder.py` and `inspector.py`.

---

---
url: https://jetpack-desktop.github.io/sdk/worker/volumes-and-network.md
description: >-
  User-directed host folder mounting via rfd and host-enforced outbound
  allowlist proxying via JETPACK_PROXY_ENDPOINT.
---

# Volumes & Userspace Networking

Sandboxed workers start with zero access to user files and zero direct access to the host network stack. JetPack provides two explicit, auditable mechanisms when a worker needs user folders or outbound APIs.

## 1. User-Directed Host Folders (`[volumes.<name>]`)

Never hardcode or request absolute host filesystem paths in `app.toml` or from browser JavaScript. Instead, declare logical volume names and access modes in `app.toml`:

```toml
[volumes.media_input]
mode = "read-only"

[volumes.media_output]
mode = "read-write"
```

### How Resolution & Persistence Work

1. **Native OS Picker (`rfd`)**: On first launch (`app.launch`), `jetpack-daemon` prompts the human user via the native OS folder picker (`Finder` / `Explorer` / `GTK Portal`) for each unconfigured volume. If the user cancels, launch aborts with `JetPackError::VolumeNotAuthorized`.
2. **Encrypted Store Caching (`ChaCha20-Poly1305`)**: Selected folders are persisted in `paired_clients.db` (`authorized_volumes(app_id, volume_name, access_mode, host_path, updated_at)`). Subsequent launches reuse the stored directory without re-prompting unless the folder was deleted/moved or the user/client requests a reset (`reset_volumes: true` or `"app.volumes.reset"`).
3. **Browser Privacy (`AppInfo`)**: The browser only receives `{ volume_name, folder_name, is_configured }` (e.g., `folder_name: "Clips"`). Full host paths are **never** sent over WebSockets.
4. **Zero Client Trust**: Any absolute host path passed by an untrusted browser in `AppLaunchRequest` is ignored/rejected.

### Accessing Mounted Volumes in Python Workers

Inside the sandbox, `jetpack-daemon` injects one environment variable per volume using the pattern `JETPACK_VOL_<UPPERCASE_NAME>`:

```python
import os
from pathlib import Path

input_dir = Path(os.environ["JETPACK_VOL_MEDIA_INPUT"])
output_dir = Path(os.environ["JETPACK_VOL_MEDIA_OUTPUT"])

# Read-only mount: reading succeeds; writing raises PermissionError / EPERM
files = sorted(p.name for p in input_dir.iterdir() if p.is_file())

# Read-write mount: writing processed artifacts succeeds
out_file = output_dir / "processed.mp4"
```

> **Note:** Volumes declared with `mode = "read-only"` are enforced as read-only by the OS kernel sandbox (`AppContainer` NTFS DACL, `Seatbelt`, or `bwrap --ro-bind` + `Landlock`), even if your user account owns the folder.

## 2. Outbound Networking via Userspace Proxy

Because workers run without direct network interfaces (`CLONE_NEWNET` on Linux, `(deny default)` on macOS, restricted capabilities on Windows), declare required remote endpoints in `[permissions].network_allowlist`:

```toml
[permissions]
model_cache = true
network_allowlist = [
  "preset:huggingface",
  # Expands to:
  # "huggingface.co:443", "*.huggingface.co:443", "hf.co:443", "*.hf.co:443", "*.xethub.hf.co:443"
]
```

### Using the Proxy in Python Workers

`jetpack-daemon` automatically sets `JETPACK_PROXY_ENDPOINT`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, and `ALL_PROXY` inside the sandboxed process environment. `jetpack_sdk.JetPackClient` exposes `client.proxy_endpoint`:

```python
import urllib.request
from jetpack_sdk import JetPackClient

with JetPackClient() as client:
    proxy_url = client.proxy_endpoint
    if proxy_url:
        handler = urllib.request.ProxyHandler({
            "http": proxy_url,
            "https": proxy_url,
        })
        opener = urllib.request.build_opener(handler)
        with opener.open("https://huggingface.co/api/models") as resp:
            data = resp.read()
```

### Streaming Downloads, Redirect Chains, and Blocked-Host Diagnostics

* **Zero-buffering multi-GB streaming**: `UserspaceProxy` enforces a `30s` upstream connect timeout without capping active transfer duration, streams tunnels with fixed `64 KiB` directional buffers (`tokio::io::copy_bidirectional_with_sizes`), and refreshes worker idle-activity heartbeats during active transfers so multi-gigabyte model downloads (Whisper, Flux, RMBG, TTS) do not trip the idle reaper.
* **Redirect-chain protection**: Supports HTTP headers up to `64 KiB` (accommodating long presigned S3/LFS CDN redirect URLs and returning `431 Request Header Fields Too Large` on overflow) and enforces `Connection: close` on plain HTTP forwarding so every hop re-validates `network_allowlist`.
* **Actionable diagnostics**: Requests to any `host:port` not matching `network_allowlist` (or targeting loopback daemon ports) are blocked immediately with `403 Forbidden`, include an `X-Jetpack-Blocked-Target: <host>:<port>` response header, and emit a `WARN` event in `<root>/logs/daemon.log` and the Developer Mode live terminal showing the exact domain/wildcard or `"preset:huggingface"` rule to add in `app.toml`.

## 3. Persistent AI Model Cache (`permissions.model_cache`)

Because per-job workspaces (`<root>/workspaces/job_<id>`) are ephemeral and app bundles (`<root>/apps/<app-id>/<version>`) are read-only and replaced on updates, heavy AI workers should opt into the shared persistent model cache in `app.toml`:

```toml
[permissions]
model_cache = true
network_allowlist = ["preset:huggingface"]
```

When `model_cache = true`:

* `jetpack-daemon` prepares `<root>/cache/models` (with `0o700` permissions on Unix) plus `huggingface/` and `torch/` subdirectories and mounts `<root>/cache/models` **read-write** into the OS sandbox (Seatbelt, AppContainer NTFS ACL, or `bwrap` + Landlock).
* The worker environment receives `JETPACK_MODEL_CACHE_DIR=<root>/cache/models`, `HF_HOME=<root>/cache/models/huggingface`, and `TORCH_HOME=<root>/cache/models/torch`.
* When `model_cache = false` (the default), `<root>/cache/models` remains inaccessible under the sandbox default-deny policy and these variables are not injected.

## 4. Isolated Persistent App Home (`JETPACK_APP_HOME` / `APP_HOME`)

Every installed application automatically receives its own private, persistent read-write data directory at `<appdata_root>/<app_id>` (`<root>/appdata/<app_id>` by default, `0o700` on Unix) without requiring any `[volumes.<name>]` declaration or native folder-picker prompt:

* **Provisioned automatically**: Created during installation (`app.pull`, `install-local`, core app seeding) and verified before every worker launch.
* **Per-app kernel isolation**: Each worker's OS sandbox grants read/write access only to its own `<appdata_root>/<app_id>` folder while keeping sibling `<appdata_root>/<other_app_id>` directories and `<appdata_root>` listings inaccessible.
* **Worker environment & Python SDK**: Inside the sandbox, `jetpack-daemon` unconditionally sets both `JETPACK_APP_HOME` and `APP_HOME` to `<appdata_root>/<app_id>`. In Python workers, `client.app_home` returns a `pathlib.Path` pointing directly to this directory:

```python
from jetpack_sdk import JetPackClient

with JetPackClient() as client:
    db_path = client.app_home / "state.sqlite3"
    db_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
```

* **User-configurable root folder**: Users can relocate `<appdata_root>` anytime under **My Hardware & Security -> App Data Folder** in Control Center (**"Choose Folder..."** invokes the daemon's main-thread native `rfd` picker; **"Reset to Default"** restores `<root>/appdata`). Uninstalling the JetPack daemon only removes internal JetPack state and leaves custom external `appdata_dir` folders untouched.

---

url: https://jetpack-desktop.github.io/publishing/manifest-reference.md

  Strict app.toml manifest schema reference covering package, hardware,
  runtimes, python_env, services, volumes, permissions, and execution.

# Manifest Reference (`app.toml`)

Every JetPack native application is governed by an `app.toml` manifest parsed into `AppManifest` (`crates/jetpack-common/src/manifest.rs`) with `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`. Any unrecognized or misspelled field fails validation immediately.

Validate any manifest locally with:

```bash
jetpack-daemon --validate-manifest path/to/app.toml
```

## Complete Annotated Example

```toml
[package]
id = "com.dev.example-worker"
name = "Example Compute Worker"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Annotated reference worker demonstrating all eight JetPack app.toml sections."
authors = ["Your Name <dev@example.com>"]
license = "MIT"
homepage = "https://example.com/jetpack-worker"

[hardware]
min_ram_mb = 512
min_vram_mb = 0
min_disk_mb = 128
accelerators = ["metal", "cuda", "cpu"]
architectures = ["darwin/arm64", "linux/amd64", "windows/amd64"]

[runtimes.python]
version = "3.12.6"
digest = "sha256:ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad"
image = "ghcr.io/jetpack/runtime-python:3.12.6"
target_dir = "runtimes/python"

[runtimes.ffmpeg]
version = "9.0.2"
target_dir = "runtimes/ffmpeg-9.0.2"

[runtimes.ffmpeg.platforms."darwin/arm64"]
url = "https://github.com/Tyrrrz/FFmpegBin/releases/download/9.0.2/ffmpeg-osx-arm64.zip"
digest = "sha256:7d22a2893ccd761c3b4214165975e306d6c85c1de188f79f7e2723070c0006e4"

[python_env]
python_version = "3.12"
requirements = ["jetpack-sdk"]
# uv_lock_sha256 = "428843fd0e0da23463920ba9aa0191a39f32a47b02e97a936c974ba996b4b98f"
isolated = true

[python_env.backend_indexes]
cuda = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124"
cpu = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu"

[services.preprocessor]
command = "bin/preprocessor.py"
args = ["--workers", "1"]
restart_policy = "on-failure"
depends_on = []

[services.preprocessor.env]
LOG_FORMAT = "compact"

[volumes.inputs]
mode = "read-only"

[volumes.outputs]
mode = "read-write"

[permissions]
gpu_access = true
model_cache = true
filesystem_scopes = ["cache"]
network_allowlist = ["preset:huggingface"]
max_memory_mb = 4096

[execution]
entrypoint = "worker.py"
args = []
# working_dir = "."
ipc_transport = "auto"
graceful_shutdown_secs = 10

[execution.env]
JETPACK_LOG_LEVEL = "info"
```

***

## Section-by-Section Reference

### 1. `[package]` (Required)

| Field | Type | Required | Validation Rules |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `id` | `string` | Yes | Matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{1,126}[a-z0-9]$`; no `..` or slashes. `io.jetpack.*` is reserved for verified catalog apps. |
| `name` | `string` | Yes | Non-empty human-readable display name. |
| `version` | `string` | Yes | Strict SemVer (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`). |
| `description` | `string` | No | Short UI description (defaults to `""`). |
| `authors` | `string[]` | No | Package author strings. |
| `license` | `string` | No | Optional SPDX license identifier. |
| `homepage` | `string` | No | Optional project homepage URL. |

### 2. `[hardware]` (Required)

| Field | Type | Required | Validation Rules |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `min_ram_mb` | `u64` | No | Minimum system RAM in MiB (`0` default). |
| `min_vram_mb` | `u64` | No | Minimum GPU VRAM in MiB (`0` default). |
| `min_disk_mb` | `u64` | No | Minimum disk space in MiB (`0` default). |
| `accelerators` | `string[]` | No | Allowed values: `cpu`, `cuda`, `metal`, `mps`, `mlx`, `rocm`, `vulkan`, `directml`. |
| `architectures` | `string[]` | Yes | Non-empty list of `windows/amd64`, `darwin/arm64`, `linux/amd64`. |

### 3. `[runtimes.<name>]` (Optional)

| Field | Type | Required | Validation Rules |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `version` | `string` | Yes | Runtime version string (e.g. `"3.12.6"`). |
| `digest` | `string` | Conditional | `sha256:<64-hex>` digest (required unless `platforms` supplies per-platform entries). |
| `image` | `string` | No | OCI artifact reference (e.g. `ghcr.io/jetpack/runtime-python:3.12.6`). |
| `url` | `string` | No | Direct HTTPS archive URL (`.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, `.zip`). |
| `platforms."<os/arch>"` | `table` | No | Per-platform `{ digest, url?, image? }` overrides keyed by `TargetPlatform`. |
| `target_dir` | `string` | Yes | Relative path inside the app bundle (no `..` or leading `/`). |

### 4. `[python_env]` (Optional)

| Field | Type | Required | Validation Rules |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `python_version` | `string` | Yes | Target Python version (e.g. `"3.12"`). |
| `requirements` | `string[]` | No | PyPI requirement specifiers (arguments starting with `-` are rejected). |
| `uv_lock_sha256` | `string` | No | 64-hex SHA-256 (or `sha256:<hex>`) verified against `uv.lock`. |
| `index_url` | `string` | No | Custom PyPI index URL. |
| `extra_index_urls` | `string[]` | No | Extra PyPI index URLs. |
| `isolated` | `bool` | No | Defaults to `true` (prevents host site-packages leakage). |
| `backend_indexes` | `map<string, string>` | No | Per-backend wheel index URLs keyed by `cuda`, `mps`, `metal`, `rocm`, or `cpu`. |

### 5. `[services.<name>]` (Optional)

| Field | Type | Required | Validation Rules |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `command` | `string` | Yes | Relative executable path inside the app bundle (no `..` or absolute paths). |
| `args` | `string[]` | No | CLI arguments for the companion service. |
| `env` | `map<string, string>` | No | Sanitized environment variables (forbidden linker vars rejected). |
| `depends_on` | `string[]` | No | Other `[services]` keys; validated with DFS cycle detection. |
| `restart_policy` | `string` | No | `"never"` (default), `"on-failure"`, or `"always"`. |
| `healthcheck_ipc` | `string` | No | Optional relative IPC healthcheck endpoint. |

### 6. `[volumes.<name>]` (Optional)

| Field | Type | Required | Validation Rules |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `mode` | `string` | Yes | `"read-only"` or `"read-write"`. Host paths are **strictly forbidden** in `app.toml`. |

### 7. `[permissions]` (Optional; Defaults to Strict Default-Deny)

| Field | Type | Default | Validation Rules |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `filesystem_scopes` | `string[]` | `[]` | Relative subdirectories inside the job workspace (no `/`, `..`, `~`, or drive prefixes). |
| `network_allowlist` | `string[]` | `[]` | Allowed `host:port` endpoints, bracketed IPv6 literals, or `"preset:huggingface"` for the Userspace Proxy (unknown `preset:*`, wildcards `*`/`0.0.0.0:*`, and loopback daemon ports rejected). |
| `gpu_access` | `bool` | `false` | Enables OS GPU driver/device access (`AGXDeviceUserClient`, `/dev/dri`, `/dev/nvidia*`, CUDA, DirectML). |
| `model_cache` | `bool` | `false` | Mounts persistent `<root>/cache/models` read-write and injects `JETPACK_MODEL_CACHE_DIR`, `HF_HOME`, and `TORCH_HOME`. |
| `max_memory_mb` | `u64` | `None` | Optional memory ceiling in MiB (must be `> 0` if set). |

### 8. `[execution]` (Required)

| Field | Type | Required | Validation Rules |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `entrypoint` | `string` | Yes | Relative path to primary script/binary inside the bundle. |
| `args` | `string[]` | No | CLI arguments passed to the entrypoint. |
| `env` | `map<string, string>` | No | Sanitized env vars. Rejects `LD_PRELOAD`, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `LD_AUDIT`, `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`, `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `DYLD_FRAMEWORK_PATH`, `PYTHONINSPECT`, `PYTHONPATH`. |
| `working_dir` | `string` | No | Optional relative working directory. |
| `ipc_transport` | `string` | No | `"auto"` (default), `"unix_socket"`, or `"named_pipe"`. |
| `timeout_secs` | `u64` | No | Optional positive hint (must be `> 0` if set); workers stay running until explicitly stopped or session/daemon shutdown. |
| `graceful_shutdown_secs` | `u64` | No | Grace period before `SIGKILL`/`TerminateProcess` (default `10`, must be `> 0`). |

---

---
url: https://jetpack-desktop.github.io/publishing/cli-tools.md
description: >-
  Reference for the console jetpack developer CLI (init, mcp, codegen, validate,
  install-local, package) and jetpack-daemon runtime/signing flags.
---

# CLI Tools Reference

JetPack provides two complementary binaries, both built together by `make release-daemon` and included in every release bundle (`JetPack.app/Contents/MacOS/` on macOS, `JetPack-windows-x64.zip` on Windows, and `JetPack-linux-x64.tar.gz` on Linux):

* **`jetpack`** (`crates/jetpack-cli`) — Standalone console developer CLI for scaffolding AI-ready projects, running the local MCP server (`stdio`), generating TypeScript opcode contracts, validating manifests, and driving local installs/packaging.
* **`jetpack-daemon`** (`crates/jetpack-daemon`) — Native system-tray orchestrator and catalog operator binary.

## Console Developer CLI (`jetpack`)

### `jetpack init <target_dir> [--app-id <id>] [--template <python|fullstack>]`

Scaffolds a ready-to-run JetPack project in `<target_dir>` with AI instructions (`AGENTS.md`, regular-file mirror `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/rules/jetpack.mdc`) and Agent Skills (`.agents/skills/create-jetpack-worker/SKILL.md`, `.agents/skills/add-binary-opcode/SKILL.md`, `.agents/skills/debug-pairing/SKILL.md`). Refuses to overwrite an existing `app.toml`.

```bash
# Python worker starter (default)
jetpack init ./workers/my-ocr-worker --template python

# Fullstack TypeScript (@jetpack/client) + Python worker starter
jetpack init ./apps/my-ai-app --app-id com.dev.my-ai-app --template fullstack
```

### `jetpack mcp`

Starts the local Model Context Protocol (MCP) server (`rmcp`) over `stdio` transport (`stdin`/`stdout` JSON-RPC, all `tracing` diagnostics directed to `stderr`). Bridges AI coding agents with embedded/local documentation (`JETPACK_DOCS_DIR` override supported) and token-authenticated `jetpack-daemon` introspection (`pairing.ipc`).

Exposes 5 tools:

* `search_docs(query, max_results?)` — Searches embedded/local JetPack SDK, security, and `app.toml` docs.
* `get_daemon_status()` — Checks daemon health, version, `127.0.0.1` WebSocket reachability, paired origins, and running workers.
* `read_worker_logs(app_id, lines?)` — Tails live or offline `worker.log` / `daemon.log` lines and crash tracebacks with sensitive token/key redaction.
* `validate_manifest(path)` — Validates `app.toml` against the current `AppManifest` schema.
* `scaffold_app(target_dir, app_id?, template?)` — Scaffolds a `python` or `fullstack` project with AI rules and Agent Skills.

### `jetpack codegen [--worker <path>] [--out <path>] [--strict]`

Parses Python worker source files or directories in pure Rust (`rustpython-parser`, zero Python runtime required) to extract Pydantic `BaseModel`, `TypedDict`, `@dataclass`, `@opcode(...)` / `client.opcode(...)` handlers, and `if opcode == ...` / `match` branches into a strict TypeScript declaration file (`jetpack-env.d.ts` exporting `JetPackOpcodeMap`):

```bash
jetpack codegen --worker worker.py --out src/jetpack-env.d.ts --strict
```

* `--worker <path>`: Python file or directory to inspect (defaults to `worker.py`).
* `--out <path>`: Output TypeScript `.d.ts` file path (defaults to `jetpack-env.d.ts`).
* `--strict`: Exit non-zero if zero opcodes are discovered.

### `jetpack validate [path]`

Validates `app.toml` (defaults to `app.toml` in the current directory, or `<dir>/app.toml` when a directory path is passed) using `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` and semantic security checks:

```bash
jetpack validate ./workers/my-ocr-worker/app.toml
```

### `jetpack install-local` (`path`)

Delegates to `jetpack-daemon --install-local-app <path>` to package and install a local developer worker (including any built `ui/` static directory) directly into `<root>/blobs/sha256/` and `<root>/apps/<app-id>/<version>/` in unverified developer mode (`is_verified = false`, restricted to `127.0.0.1` / `localhost`). Defaults `path` to `.`.

### `jetpack package` (`path --out <bundle_dir> --oci-ref <ref>`)

Delegates to `jetpack-daemon --package-app` to package a validated project—alongside its built `ui/` static frontend (`ui/index.html`, `ui/assets/*`) if present—into an OCI Image Layout v1.0.0 bundle (automatically excluding `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `.agents/`, `jetpack-env.d.ts`, `node_modules/`, `target/`, `.git/`, `.venv/`, `__pycache__/`, symlinks, and secret files). Defaults `path` to `.`.

***

## Daemon Developer & Publisher Flags (`jetpack-daemon`)

### `--init-app <target_dir>`

Scaffolds a ready-to-run starter Python worker project in `<target_dir>` using the same shared template builder as `jetpack init` (including `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/rules/jetpack.mdc`, and `.agents/skills/`, and refusing to overwrite an existing `app.toml`):

```bash
jetpack-daemon --init-app ./workers/my-ocr-worker
```

Creates:

* `app.toml` — Validated starter manifest using a non-official `com.dev.<slug>` ID (`com.dev.my-ocr-worker`).
* `worker.py` — Executable (`0755` on Unix) Python worker using `jetpack_sdk.JetPackClient`.
* `pyproject.toml` — Project metadata (`requires-python = ">=3.12"`, `jetpack-sdk` dependency).
* `README.md` — Project-specific validation, local install, and packaging commands.
* `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/rules/jetpack.mdc`, and `.agents/skills/*` — AI agent instructions and workflows (automatically excluded from OCI packaging).

### `--validate-manifest <path>`

Parses an `app.toml` file with `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` and runs all semantic and security checks:

```bash
jetpack-daemon --validate-manifest ./workers/my-ocr-worker/app.toml
```

### `--install-local-app <source_dir>`

Validates, packages, and installs a local developer worker (plus any `ui/` bundle) directly into `<root>/blobs/sha256/` and `<root>/apps/<app-id>/<version>/` in unverified developer mode (`is_verified = false`):

```bash
jetpack-daemon --install-local-app ./workers/my-ocr-worker
```

* Blocks official `SignedAppCatalog` IDs (`APP_SPOOFING_DETECTED`).
* Displays the app with an `UNVERIFIED / LOCAL DEV` badge in Control Center, automatically discovers `<root>/apps/<app-id>/<version>/ui/index.html` for `/apps/<app-id>/`, and restricts WebSocket origins to `127.0.0.1` / `localhost`.

### `--package-app <source_dir> --out <bundle_dir> [--oci-ref <ref>]`

Packages a validated worker directory (including optional `ui/` static assets served dynamically at `/apps/<app-id>/`) into an ORAS-compatible **OCI Image Layout v1.0.0** directory (`index.json` with `org.opencontainers.image.ref.name`) and prints `manifest_sha256`, the `oras cp --from-oci-layout` push command, `oras manifest fetch --descriptor` digest check, and a `CatalogAppEntry` JSON snippet:

```bash
jetpack-daemon \
  --package-app ./workers/my-ocr-worker \
  --out ./dist/my-ocr-worker-oci \
  --oci-ref ghcr.io/your-org/my-ocr-worker:0.1.0
```

Automatically strips `*.key`, `*.pem`, `*.secret`, `jetpack-root-signing*`, `node_modules/`, `target/`, `.git/`, `.venv/`, `__pycache__/`, and symlinks so build caches, secrets, and unsafe links cannot leak into published layers.

## Catalog Operator Commands

### `--generate-catalog-keypair --out-priv <path>`

Generates an `Ed25519` root keypair using `OsRng`:

```bash
jetpack-daemon --generate-catalog-keypair --out-priv ~/.secrets/jetpack-root-signing.key
```

* Writes the 32-byte seed (64 lowercase hex characters) atomically (`create_new(true)`) with mode `0600` on Unix.
* Prints only the public key hex and the Rust `CATALOG_VERIFY_PUBKEY` literal to stdout.

### `--sign-catalog <catalog_json_path> [--key <priv_key_path>]`

Canonicalizes `SignedAppCatalog`, signs it with `Ed25519` (reading `--key` or `JETPACK_SIGNING_KEY`), writes `ed25519_signature` atomically, and immediately re-verifies the file from disk:

```bash
jetpack-daemon --sign-catalog crates/jetpack-daemon/assets/catalog.signed.json --key ~/.secrets/jetpack-root-signing.key
```

## Runtime, Inspection & Diagnostic Flags

| Flag | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| `--version, -V` | Print the compiled `jetpack-daemon` semantic version and exit cleanly. |
| `--headless` | Run `jetpack-daemon` without a desktop system tray icon (CI / server). |
| `--seed-core-apps` | Package and pre-install curated core workers from `examples/` (e.g., slim release bundle `examples/ffmpeg-media-converter`, excluding `.venv`, `__pycache__`, `tests`, and media files) into CAS and `<root>/apps/`. |
| `--export-diagnostics [--out <path>]` | Collect a sanitized `.zip` diagnostic bundle (`diagnostics.json` + redacted `daemon.log` tail) and write it to `<path>` or `<root>/logs/jetpack-diagnostics-<timestamp>.zip`. |
| `--print-hardware-profile` | Probe CPU topology, RAM/unified memory, and GPUs (`NVML`, `Vulkan`, `DX12`, `Metal`). |
| `--list-paired-clients` | List approved origins and client UUIDs stored in `paired_clients.db`. |
| `--list-installed-apps` | Scan `<root>/apps/` and print discovered manifests and versions. |
| `--register-uri-scheme` | Register `jetpack://` and `corenode://` custom URL schemes in user space. |
| `--generate-test-pair-uri` | Print a deterministic test `jetpack://pair` URI and SHA-256 fingerprint. |
| `--test-ws-client` | Connect to a running daemon (`127.0.0.1:9470`) to verify PNA, handshake, and `system.echo` (supports `--send-json` and `--origin`). |
| `--ws-smoke-test` | Run offline end-to-end WebSocket security and `hardware.get_profile` smoke test. |
| `--oci-smoke-test` | Run offline OCI CAS, SHA-256 verification, and hardlink/APFS clone smoke test. |
| `--oci-remote-smoke-test <ref> [--expected-digest <sha256:...>]` | Pull a live public OCI reference (such as `ghcr.io/...`), verify manifest + blob SHA-256 digests, and safely unpack into an isolated temporary CAS root. |
| `--python-smoke-test` | Run offline hermetic `uv` + `python-build-standalone` provisioner smoke test. |
| `--sandbox-smoke-test` | Run offline OS native kernel sandbox (`AppContainer` / `Seatbelt` / `bwrap+Landlock`) smoke test. |
| `--worker-ipc-smoke-test` | Run offline sandboxed worker IPC, userspace proxy, and lifecycle cleanup smoke test. |
| `--full-e2e-smoke-test` | Run the full end-to-end orchestrator, sandbox, GPU worker, and WebSocket integration test. |
| `--background` | Hidden internal flag omitted from `--help`; passed by OS autostart entries (`LaunchAgents`, `HKCU\...\Run`, XDG `.desktop`) to suppress auto-opening the Control Center window at OS login. |
| `--cleanup-old-binary <path>` | Hidden internal post-update flag spawned by the self-updater; validates a `.old` suffix and removes the previous binary or `.app.old` bundle asynchronously (`10 × 200ms` retries). |

---

---
url: https://jetpack-desktop.github.io/publishing/sdk-publishing.md
description: >-
  Build, verify in isolated consumers, synchronize versions, and publish
  @jetpack/client (NPM) and jetpack-sdk (PyPI).
---

# SDK Publishing (NPM & PyPI)

Maintainers can build, verify in clean isolated environments, synchronize versions, and publish both official JetPack SDKs using repeatable user-space `Makefile` commands:

* **Frontend SDK (`@jetpack/client`)** — `web/packages/jetpack-client`, bundling compiled `jetpack-wasm` (`crates/jetpack-wasm`) into `wasm/` and re-exporting it via `@jetpack/client/wasm` so external consumers require zero manual WASM path setup.
* **Python Worker SDK (`jetpack-sdk`)** — `sdks/python`, built with `hatchling` (`sdist` + `py3-none-any` wheel) with zero mandatory dependencies (`dependencies = []`) and optional `msgpack` acceleration (`jetpack-sdk[msgpack]`).

See [Frontend Quickstart](/sdk/frontend/quickstart) and [Python Worker SDK](/sdk/worker/python-sdk) for consumer usage.

## 1. Build Both SDKs (`make sdk-build`)

```bash
make sdk-build
```

`make sdk-build` executes in user space:

1. Compiles `crates/jetpack-wasm` via `wasm-pack --target web` (`make wasm`).
2. Copies compiled WASM glue and binaries (`jetpack_wasm.js`, `jetpack_wasm.d.ts`, `jetpack_wasm_bg.wasm`, `jetpack_wasm_bg.wasm.d.ts`) into `web/packages/jetpack-client/wasm/` and compiles TypeScript to `dist/`.
3. Cleans `sdks/python/dist/` and builds fresh `.tar.gz` (`sdist`) and `.whl` (`wheel`) packages via `uv build --directory sdks/python` (or `python3 -m build`).

## 2. Verify Packaging & Isolated Consumers (`make sdk-check`)

```bash
make sdk-check
```

`make sdk-check` runs `make sdk-build` and executes `scripts/sdk_check.sh`, verifying:

1. **Version Parity**: `@jetpack/client` (`package.json`), `jetpack-sdk` (`pyproject.toml` PEP 440), and `EMBEDDED_JETPACK_SDK_VERSION` (`crates/jetpack-daemon/src/python.rs`) match.
2. **TypeScript SDK Unit Tests & Tarball Inspection**: Runs `npm --prefix web/packages/jetpack-client test`, packs the `.tgz`, and verifies `dist/`, `wasm/`, `README.md`, and `LICENSE` are present without leaking `src/`, `tests/`, or `node_modules/`.
3. **Isolated Vite + TypeScript Consumer Smoke Check**: Installs the packed `.tgz` into a fresh temporary Vite + TypeScript project, verifies `tsc --noEmit` and `vite build` emit `jetpack_wasm_bg-*.wasm` into `dist/assets/`, and confirms `vite dev` serves `/node_modules/@jetpack/client/wasm/jetpack_wasm_bg.wasm` with `200 OK` and `application/wasm`.
4. **Python Metadata & Isolated Venv Check**: Runs `twine check sdks/python/dist/*`, inspects `.whl` contents (including `jetpack_sdk/py.typed`), installs the wheel into a clean temporary `uv venv` without host site-packages, and passes `sdks/python/tests`.

## 3. Version Synchronization (`scripts/sync_version.sh`)

Before tagging a release, synchronize all workspace and SDK manifests from a single semantic version or tag:

```bash
bash scripts/sync_version.sh v0.2.0
```

This updates `Cargo.toml`, `crates/jetpack-daemon/assets/Info.plist`, `web/package.json`, `web/packages/jetpack-client/package.json`, `sdks/python/pyproject.toml` (converting SemVer pre-release tags such as `-alpha.1` to PEP 440 `a1`), and `EMBEDDED_JETPACK_SDK_VERSION` in `crates/jetpack-daemon/src/python.rs`.

## 4. Dry-Run & Live Publishing (`make sdk-publish`)

Always run a non-mutating dry run before publishing:

```bash
make sdk-publish DRY_RUN=1
```

`DRY_RUN=1` validates the full `make sdk-check` suite, runs `npm publish ./web/packages/jetpack-client --access public --dry-run`, checks `sdks/python/dist/*` with `twine check`, and skips live uploads (even on a dirty git tree).

When publishing live from a clean git working tree:

| Command | Target Registry | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `make sdk-publish` | NPM + PyPI | Fails if git tree is dirty unless `ALLOW_DIRTY=1` is set |
| `make sdk-publish-npm` | NPM only (`@jetpack/client`) | Runs `sdk-check` first |
| `make sdk-publish-pypi` | PyPI only (`jetpack-sdk`) | Runs `sdk-check` first |

### Authentication Options

* **NPM (`@jetpack/client`)**: Set `NPM_TOKEN` (or `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`)—written to an ephemeral `0600` temporary config deleted on exit without modifying `~/.npmrc`—or log in beforehand via `npm login`.
* **PyPI (`jetpack-sdk`)**: Set `UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN` (or `PYPI_API_TOKEN` / `TWINE_PASSWORD`), or rely on `~/.pypirc` / an interactive prompt.

```bash
# Non-interactive CI / token-based publish
NPM_TOKEN=... UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN=... make sdk-publish

# Allow publishing while testing uncommitted local edits (not recommended for releases)
ALLOW_DIRTY=1 make sdk-publish-npm
```

## 5. GitHub Actions Release Integration

`.github/workflows/release.yml` runs `sdk-check` on every tag (`v*`) or manual `workflow_dispatch` run, gating public desktop releases on SDK packaging verification. When `NPM_TOKEN` and/or `PYPI_API_TOKEN` repository secrets are configured, the `publish-sdks` job publishes both packages automatically after release artifacts succeed; if either secret is omitted, the step logs an informational notice and skips cleanly without failing binary or GitHub Pages releases.

See also [CLI Tools Reference](/publishing/cli-tools) and [Store Submission & Catalog Signing](/publishing/store-submission).

---

---
url: https://jetpack-desktop.github.io/publishing/store-submission.md
description: >-
  Package validated workers into multi-arch OCI Image Layout bundles, push to
  registries, and sign catalog.signed.json with Ed25519.
---

# Store Submission & Catalog Signing

This guide covers packaging a validated worker as a multi-arch OCI Image Layout bundle, pushing it to an OCI registry (`ghcr.io`, Docker Hub, etc.), and signing `catalog.signed.json` as a JetPack platform operator.

## 1. Developer Workflow: Packaging & Pushing to OCI

### Step 1: Validate Your Manifest

Ensure `app.toml` passes strict schema and security checks:

```bash
jetpack-daemon --validate-manifest ./workers/my-ocr-worker/app.toml
```

### Step 2: Package an OCI Image Layout v1.0.0 Bundle

```bash
jetpack package ./workers/my-ocr-worker \
  --out ./dist/my-ocr-worker-oci \
  --oci-ref ghcr.io/your-org/my-ocr-worker:0.1.0
```

*(Equivalent daemon invocation: `jetpack-daemon --package-app ./workers/my-ocr-worker --out ./dist/my-ocr-worker-oci --oci-ref ghcr.io/your-org/my-ocr-worker:0.1.0`.)*

Output bundle structure:

```text
dist/my-ocr-worker-oci/
├── oci-layout               # { "imageLayoutVersion": "1.0.0" }
├── index.json               # Root entry with org.opencontainers.image.ref.name tag annotation
└── blobs/sha256/
    ├── <layer_sha256>       # Deterministic .tar.gz with POSIX '/' paths, 0755 entrypoints
    ├── <config_sha256>      # OCI image config JSON with rootfs.diff_ids & io.jetpack.app.* labels
    ├── <manifest_sha256>... # Per-platform OciImageManifest blobs
    └── <index_sha256>       # Multi-arch OciImageIndex blob (when multiple architectures are declared)
```

The command prints `manifest_sha256`, the ready-to-run `oras cp --from-oci-layout` push command, `oras manifest fetch --descriptor` verification command, and a `CatalogAppEntry` JSON block to stdout.

### Step 3: Push to `ghcr.io` with `oras` & Verify Digest

Ensure your GHCR package visibility is set to **Public** (JetPack Store installs pull anonymously via `ghcr.io/token`), then push using the exact tag printed by `jetpack package`:

```bash
oras cp --from-oci-layout ./dist/my-ocr-worker-oci:0.1.0 ghcr.io/your-org/my-ocr-worker:0.1.0
oras manifest fetch --descriptor ghcr.io/your-org/my-ocr-worker:0.1.0
```

> **Important:** Confirm that the remote `digest` printed by `oras manifest fetch --descriptor` matches `manifest_sha256` from `jetpack package`. If your registry or push tool re-serializes the manifest or index, update `manifest_sha256` in `CatalogAppEntry` to match the exact remote digest before signing the catalog.

Verify end-to-end anonymous pull, SHA-256 verification, and Tar-Slip-safe unpacking from `ghcr.io`:

```bash
jetpack-daemon \
  --oci-remote-smoke-test ghcr.io/your-org/my-ocr-worker:0.1.0 \
  --expected-digest sha256:<64-hex>
```

For CI/CD automation, see [GitHub Actions Publishing to GHCR](/publishing/ghcr-workflow) (`examples/publish-app-ghcr.yml`).

Populate `category`, `icon_svg`, and `allowed_origins` (for example `["https://studio.example.com"]`) in the `CatalogAppEntry` JSON object.

***

## 2. Platform Operator Workflow: Key Hygiene & Catalog Signing

### Secret Hygiene & `.gitignore` Protections

Never commit private signing keys, PEM files, or seed material to source control. The repository `.gitignore` blocks:

```text
*.key
*.pem
*.secret
jetpack-root-signing*
```

Verify ignore rules before storing local test keys:

```bash
git check-ignore -v jetpack-root-signing.key test.pem catalog.secret
```

### Generating the Ed25519 Root Keypair

```bash
jetpack-daemon \
  --generate-catalog-keypair \
  --out-priv ~/.secrets/jetpack-root-signing.key
```

Security guarantees:

* **Atomic creation**: Uses `OpenOptions::create_new(true)` and refuses to overwrite existing files.
* **Strict file permissions**: Sets `0600` (`rw-------`) on macOS and Linux. On Windows, store the key under `%USERPROFILE%\.secrets\` with user-only NTFS ACLs (`icacls <path> /inheritance:r /grant:r "%USERNAME%:F"`).
* **Zero-exposure output**: The private seed is zeroized in memory (`zeroize::Zeroizing`) and never printed to stdout.

### Rotating `CATALOG_VERIFY_PUBKEY`

1. Store the production seed in an offline hardware vault (YubiKey, 1Password, HashiCorp Vault, or AWS KMS/Secrets Manager).
2. Paste the printed `[u8; 32]` array literal into `CATALOG_VERIFY_PUBKEY` inside `crates/jetpack-daemon/src/catalog.rs`.
3. Re-sign `crates/jetpack-daemon/assets/catalog.signed.json`.
4. Run `cargo test -p jetpack-daemon catalog::tests` to confirm `embedded_signed_catalog_verifies_against_platform_pubkey` passes, then rebuild `make release-daemon`.

### Signing `catalog.signed.json`

Sign locally using `--key` or in CI/CD via `JETPACK_SIGNING_KEY`:

```bash
# Option A: Sign using a local private seed file (64-char hex or raw 32-byte binary)
jetpack-daemon \
  --sign-catalog crates/jetpack-daemon/assets/catalog.signed.json \
  --key ~/.secrets/jetpack-root-signing.key

# Option B: Sign in CI/CD using an encrypted masked secret environment variable
export JETPACK_SIGNING_KEY="$(cat ~/.secrets/jetpack-root-signing.key)"
jetpack-daemon --sign-catalog crates/jetpack-daemon/assets/catalog.signed.json
unset JETPACK_SIGNING_KEY
```

`--sign-catalog` parses the catalog against `SignedAppCatalog` (`#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`), computes the canonical `Ed25519` signature over `SignedAppCatalog::canonical_payload_bytes()`, writes `ed25519_signature` atomically, and re-verifies the file from disk before exiting `0`.
